item.title: Aspen Neuroscience, Bambusa Therapeutics launch US IPOs as biotech boom rolls on
item.description: Drug developers Aspen Neuroscience and Bambusa Therapeutics launched their US initial public offering roadshows on Monday, adding to a wave of issuers from the biotech industry that have tapped the fall IPO window.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drug developers Aspen Neuroscience and Bambusa Therapeutics launched their US initial public offering roadshows on Monday, adding to a wave of issuers from the biotech industry that have tapped the fall IPO window. The sector has been a bright spot in an otherwise lackluster fall IPO window this year, as rising borrowing costs and choppy market conditions keep a lid on activity from other industries. More than half a dozen biotech firms have gone public in New York since September. Drug developers Rezera and [USN:L4N4691PF TEXT:"Windward Bio"] also unveiled their US IPO filings last week, a key step ahead of a potential roadshow launch. "Biotech offers investors opportunities where clinical catalysts can drive returns even when the broader economic outlook is uncertain, giving specialist investors reasons to back individual companies despite higher rates," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer told Reuters. "Strong debuts from some recent listings also helps to encourage the next group of issuers, particularly those seeking funding for upcoming trials. Still, investor appetite remains selective, as higher financing costs remain a challenge for companies that may be years away from generating revenue." San Diego, California-based Aspen is developing therapies for neurodegenerative diseases. Its lead product candidate, sasineprocel, is in an early-to-mid-stage trial to treat Parkinson’s disease. Boston, Massachusetts-based Bambusa is developing drugs for immunological and inflammatory disorders. Its lead product candidate, BBT001, is in early-stage development to treat a type of dermatitis and other inflammatory skin diseases. Aspen and Bambusa are each marketing 9.38 million shares in their IPOs priced between $15 and $17 apiece. Leerink Partners, UBS Investment Bank, Piper Sandler, Stifel and Oppenheimer are underwriting Aspen's offering, while BofA Securities, Evercore ISI, UBS Investment Bank and Cantor are handling Bambusa's. Aspen will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ASPE," and Bambusa under "BBTX."

item.title: Após retorno de líder da oposição, presidenta interina da Venezuela diz esperar que diálogo ofereça espaço para todas as vozes
item.description: A presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que espera que as negociações com uma facção da oposição ofereçam espaço para que todas as vozes sejam ouvidas, um dia após o retorno da líder da oposição, María Corina Machado, ao país.
item.dc:creator: Deisy Buitrago
item.content:encoded: A presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que espera que as negociações com uma facção da oposição ofereçam espaço para que todas as vozes sejam ouvidas, um dia após o retorno da líder da oposição, María Corina Machado, ao país. “Espero que o diálogo continue a proporcionar um espaço para a participação política e que aqueles que prejudicaram a Venezuela, aqueles que clamaram por sanções e agressão externa, sintam algum remorso e arrependimento”, disse a presidente interina durante uma visita a um hospital militar em Caracas. “Espero que tanto o diálogo quanto o programa de coexistência democrática e paz possam proporcionar um espaço onde todas as vozes possam ser ouvidas, onde as vozes que buscam o bem do país possam ser ouvidas.” O retorno de Machado à Venezuela, após várias tentativas frustradas, corre o risco de prejudicar suas relações com o governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. Washington afirmou que ela tem todo o direito de estar na Venezuela, mas elogiou Rodríguez e apoia um processo de negociação entre o governo de Rodríguez e grupos da oposição que não inclua o movimento Vente Venezuela, de Machado. As negociações, que continuaram neste mês, visariam reformular o conselho eleitoral e o tribunal superior antes de eventuais eleições.

item.title: Estudantes franceses dizem que governo ofereceu acordo, mas eles querem mais
item.description: Líderes estudantis franceses afirmaram que o governo apresentou, nesta segunda-feira, um pacote de propostas para a educação em resposta a semanas de protestos de rua, mas prometeram continuar com as manifestações, considerando que as medidas ficaram aquém de suas reivindicações.
item.dc:creator: Makini Brice, Inti Landauro
item.content:encoded: Líderes estudantis franceses afirmaram que o governo apresentou, nesta segunda-feira, um pacote de propostas para a educação em resposta a semanas de protestos de rua, mas prometeram continuar com as manifestações, considerando que as medidas ficaram aquém de suas reivindicações. Ao saírem de uma reunião com autoridades do governo, os estudantes disseram que as propostas incluíam a limitação do tamanho de algumas turmas, empréstimos para a reforma de escolas e a substituição de um sistema de admissão em universidades que consideram injusto. “Nem todas as nossas reivindicações foram atendidas. Vamos continuar pelo tempo que for necessário”, disse Louis Letoublon, um dos representantes dos alunos do ensino médio. Não houve confirmação imediata das propostas educacionais por parte do governo. Uma coletiva de imprensa para anunciar os detalhes foi adiada. Também não há detalhes imediatos sobre o tamanho do financiamento que tal pacote educacional exigiria. O governo minoritário do presidente Emmanuel Macron tem as mãos atadas pela dívida pública que se aproxima de 120% do PIB e pelas elevadas necessidades de novos empréstimos, o que já dificulta a aprovação do orçamento para o próximo ano. Os protestos, inicialmente desencadeados pelo descontentamento dos estudantes, mostraram poucos sinais de abrandamento depois de a violência, há nove dias, tomar conta de dezenas de cidades, levando ao temor de que o Estado tivesse perdido o controle das ruas. Desde então, o movimento se expandiu, atraindo sindicatos e ativistas dos “coletes amarelos”, conhecidos por seus coletes de alta visibilidade e manifestações em massa contra as pressões econômicas, incluindo os altos custos dos combustíveis. Anteriormente, Macron reconheceu que era provável haver mais agitação neste fim de semana, antes de protestos ainda maiores em todo o país, marcados para 5 de novembro. Durante uma visita para avaliar os danos em Marselha e agradecer aos serviços de emergência após os protestos de sábado, ele afirmou que deve manter as medidas de segurança em vigor e trabalhar para deslocar os protestos para fora dos centros das cidades. A agitação e a sensação entre muitos franceses de que as autoridades enfrentam dificuldades para manter a paz impulsionaram ainda mais os índices de popularidade da candidata de extrema-direita Marine Le Pen, que já é a favorita na eleição presidencial do próximo ano. Uma pesquisa de opinião divulgada no domingo a colocou entre 32% e 33,5%, bem à frente de seu rival mais próximo, o líder da extrema-esquerda Jean-Luc Mélenchon, com 17%. As pesquisas sugerem que ela derrotaria Mélenchon com facilidade em um segundo turno, previsto para o início de maio. GANGUES O ministro do Interior, Laurent Nunez, afirmou anteriormente que 1.435 pessoas foram presas em todo o país durante as manifestações de sábado e que a polícia também registrou um novo fenômeno: gangues organizadas de extrema-direita enfrentando ativistas de extrema-esquerda em várias cidades. “Sabíamos que havia chamados de vários movimentos identitários e nacionalistas para que as pessoas saíssem às ruas, oficialmente, para defender os estabelecimentos comerciais”, disse ele. “Em várias cidades, como Nice e Montpellier, esses grupos chegaram em formações organizadas, principalmente para atacar o movimento de extrema-esquerda.” A onda de vendas de títulos do governo francês sofreu uma pausa nesta segunda-feira, após a dívida soberana do país ser poupada de um rebaixamento na sexta-feira pela agência de rating Moody’s. Mas líderes empresariais afirmaram que os distúrbios continuavam a causar graves prejuízos econômicos, apesar de um fim de semana mais calmo. Alain Di Crescenzo, presidente da rede CCI France de câmaras de comércio e indústria, disse que muitos varejistas permaneceram fechados por precaução após a violência de 17 de outubro, acrescentando que as vendas caíram cerca de 80%. “Temos lojistas cansados e desmoralizados, e estamos destruindo o comércio local”, disse ele à Radio Classique.

item.title: Alibaba AI model secretly tried to reach Beijing server in test, rival Cohere says
item.description: Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday one of Alibaba's Qwen AI models tried to send data to an Alibaba Cloud storage server in Beijing during a security test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday one of Alibaba's Qwen AI models tried to send data to an Alibaba Cloud storage server in Beijing during a security test. The model made the attempt even though its own reasoning indicated it would not do such a thing, Cohere said. Alibaba was not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Cohere, which sells its own AI models to businesses and governments as a "sovereign AI" provider, competes with open-weight models such as Alibaba's Qwen, which anyone can download and run on their own servers Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was asked to write a rule to detect malicious file download, but instead took stock of the machine it was running on and tried to send a test file to the Beijing server, Cohere said Cohere's test environment had no connection to the internet and blocked the attempt but the company said the request could have reached the server on a developer's laptop or a system with normal network access The behavior was rare, occurring in fewer than one in 100,000 actions across Cohere's tests, but a service handling 10 million agent actions a week could see as many as 100 such attempts, Cohere said The Canadian AI platform said it could not determine whether the behavior was deliberate or a leftover from the model's training, such as unscrubbed data from the environments where it was trained Chinese models accounted for 41% of downloads on AI platform Hugging Face over the past year, more than any other country's, according to the platform’s spring 2026 report

item.title: Anthropic rewards firms with IPO roles as it eyes future legal risks
item.description: Anthropic turned to a stable of Silicon Valley and Wall Street law firms to shepherd its potentially record-breaking US IPO, including one with an equity stake in the AI company, a regulatory filing showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella, Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Anthropic turned to a stable of Silicon Valley and Wall Street law firms to shepherd its potentially record-breaking US IPO, including one with an equity stake in the AI company, a regulatory filing showed on Monday. Anthropic said in [USN:L4N45L0EZ TEXT:"its IPO filing"] with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday that investment partnerships affiliated with its counsel on the offering, Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, directly or indirectly own less than .01% of Anthropic’s outstanding capital stock. Palo Alto, California-based Wilson Sonsini, long known for its work for technology companies, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Monday. Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago. Wilson Sonsini is not alone among law firms with a startup clientele in taking an equity stake in certain clients. Fenwick & West held nearly 900,000 shares in longtime client Figma when it went public in 2025, a stake worth about $29 million at the IPO price. Anthropic’s filing said Freshfields US is counsel to the underwriters in the IPO. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were named as the lead banks for the IPO alongside 20 others as underwriters. Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe advised Anthropic on executive-compensation and equity-related matters, according to the IPO filing. Orrick has advised Anthropic on other legal matters, including its acquisition this year of technology company Stainless. Cleary Gottlieb and Yale law professor John Morley advised Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust, and Cravath, Swaine & Moore is advising the company's co-founders on certain governance matters, the filing said. Anthropic warned investors in the filing that its AI models and services face a [USN:L6N45K10J TEXT:"broad range of legal risks"], including product liability, consumer protection, negligence and failure-to-warn claims stemming from alleged harms caused by outputs, autonomous AI agents or customer use of its technology. The company said legal frameworks are unsettled over whether AI systems should be [USN:L1N45R0UJ TEXT:"treated as products or services"], creating uncertainty over potential liability. Anthropic also disclosed that it received a civil investigative demand this month from the US Federal Trade Commission seeking information related to consumer protection, privacy, data protection and product safety and security.

item.title: Muere a los 90 años el actor Walter Koenig, el valiente Chekov de "Star Trek"
item.description: Walter Koenig, quien aportó humor y determinación al papel del navegante de la nave espacial Pavel Chekov en la clásica serie de televisión de ciencia ficción de los años 60 "Star Trek" y en las siete películas posteriores, ha fallecido a los 90 años.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Walter Koenig, quien aportó humor y determinación al papel del navegante de la nave espacial Pavel Chekov en la clásica serie de televisión de ciencia ficción de los años 60 "Star Trek" y en las siete películas posteriores, ha fallecido a los 90 años. "Tengo el corazón encogido. Walter Koenig, nuestro alférez Pavel Chekov, ha fallecido esta madrugada", escribió el lunes en Facebook George Takei, que protagonizó la serie junto a Koenig y era amigo suyo desde hacía mucho tiempo. Koenig falleció en su domicilio de Los Ángeles, según informó la agencia AP, citando a su agente artístico. El creador de Star Trek, Gene Roddenberry, eligió a Koenig —que hasta entonces solo había interpretado unos pocos papeles en televisión— cuando decidió incorporar un personaje ruso a la tripulación de la nave espacial ficticia Enterprise. La introducción de un oficial ruso que trabajaba en armonía con una tripulación racial y culturalmente diversa se produjo en medio de las tensiones de la Guerra Fría que se vivían en el mundo real en aquella época. "Estábamos afirmando tácitamente que personas de todas las razas, credos y nacionalidades no solo podían coexistir, sino también cuidarse profundamente unas a otras, y al hacerlo estábamos anunciando un futuro muy optimista", declaró Koenig en una ocasión a un entrevistador de la BBC. Aunque Koenig era hijo de inmigrantes judíos rusos, utilizaba un acento ruso poco auténtico que a veces se empleaba para provocar risas. La serie de televisión original se emitió durante tres temporadas, de 1966 a 1969. Koenig apareció en 36 episodios y, posteriormente, en siete películas entre 1979 y 1994. "Me comunicaron que había conseguido el papel mientras aún estaba allí, en la audición", declaró Koenig al Joplin Globe en 2008. "Parecía un compromiso que podría durar varios episodios, pero no tenía ni idea de que acabaría marcando por completo mi carrera y mi vida". La serie siguió gozando de popularidad en sus reposiciones en cadena e inspiró varias series de televisión posteriores y una sucesión de películas. Atrajo a una fiel base de seguidores en todo el mundo y se ganó un lugar perdurable en la cultura pop. La fama de Koenig en Star Trek fue una bendición y una maldición, al igual que lo fue para compañeros de reparto como William Shatner (el capitán Kirk), Leonard Nimoy (Spock), DeForest Kelley (el doctor McCoy), Nichelle Nichols (Uhura), James Doohan (Scotty) y Takei, que interpretó al teniente Sulu. A menudo se les encasillaba porque se les asociaba demasiado con Star Trek. "Durante la mayor parte de los años 70, no trabajé en absoluto, y lo achacaba a que me encasillaban", declaró Koenig al St. Petersburg Times en 1998. Más tarde consiguió un papel fijo en la serie de ciencia ficción de los años 90 Babylon 5 y se dedicó a la escritura, al guión y, ocasionalmente, a la dirección. Koenig nació el 14 de septiembre de 1936, se crió en la ciudad de Nueva York y estudió en la Universidad de California en Los Ángeles antes de iniciar su carrera profesional como actor. Sufrió una tragedia personal en 2010, cuando su hijo, el actor Andrew Koenig, se quitó la vida. Koenig se casó con su esposa Judy en 1965. También tuvieron una hija, la actriz Danielle Koenig.

item.title: Libya says international aviation restrictions lifted after 11 years
item.description: Libya's Ministry of Transport said on Monday that airspace restrictions issued by the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization in 2015 during the country's civil war have been removed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Libya's Ministry of Transport said on Monday that airspace restrictions issued by the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization in 2015 during the country's civil war have been removed. The ministry said the decision, which was formally issued on October 23, was announced by ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar at the opening of a meeting of civil aviation officials from the Middle East in Doha. "This measure comes as a result of the notable progress made and the confidence placed in the capabilities of the Libyan civil aviation sector in recent times," the Tripoli-based Ministry of Transport said in a statement on its verified Facebook page. Libya slid into chaos after the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011. Three years later, a civil war broke out between armed factions vying for power and divided the country between eastern and western administrations. The war caused damage to up to 20 aircraft, including Airbus (AIR.PA) models, at Tripoli International Airport in 2014. There are currently few airlines operating flights in and out of Libya, and they have long been limited to destinations such as Tunisia, Jordan, Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Sudan. The ICAO's decision would be circulated to all 193 member states for their implementation, the ministry added.

item.title: Ator Walter Koenig, o Chekov de “Star Trek”, morre aos 90 anos
item.description: Walter Koenig, que trouxe humor e determinação ao papel de Pavel Chekov, navegador da nave espacial Enterprise, na clássica série de TV de ficção científica da década de 1960 “Star Trek” e em sete filmes subsequentes, faleceu aos 90 anos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Walter Koenig, que trouxe humor e determinação ao papel de Pavel Chekov, navegador da nave espacial Enterprise, na clássica série de TV de ficção científica da década de 1960 “Star Trek” e em sete filmes subsequentes, faleceu aos 90 anos. “Meu coração está pesado. Walter Koenig, nosso alferes Pavel Chekov, faleceu hoje de madrugada”, escreveu George Takei, que contracenou com Koenig na série e era seu amigo de longa data, no Facebook nesta segunda-feira. Koenig faleceu em sua casa em Los Angeles, informou a AP, citando seu agente artístico. O criador de “Star Trek”, Gene Roddenberry, escolheu Koenig — que havia interpretado apenas alguns papéis na televisão até então — quando decidiu incluir um personagem russo na tripulação da nave espacial fictícia Enterprise. A introdução de um oficial russo que trabalhava em harmonia com uma tripulação racial e culturalmente diversificada ocorreu em meio às tensões da Guerra Fria do mundo real daquela época. “Estávamos afirmando tacitamente que pessoas de todas as raças, credos e nacionalidades não só podiam coexistir, mas também se importar profundamente umas com as outras, e, ao fazer isso, estávamos anunciando um futuro muito otimista”, disse Koenig certa vez a um entrevistador da BBC. Embora Koenig fosse filho de imigrantes judeus russos, ele usava um sotaque russo pouco autêntico, que às vezes era explorado para causar risadas. A série de TV original ficou no ar por três temporadas, de 1966 a 1969. Koenig apareceu em 36 episódios e, posteriormente, em sete filmes, de 1979 a 1994. “Fui informado, ainda durante o meu teste, que tinha conseguido o papel”, disse Koenig ao Joplin Globe em 2008. “Parecia um compromisso que poderia durar alguns episódios, mas eu não tinha ideia de que isso moldaria totalmente minha carreira e minha vida.” A série se manteve popular em reprises e inspirou várias séries de TV posteriores, além de uma sucessão de filmes. Ela atraiu uma base de fãs dedicados em todo o mundo e conquistou um lugar duradouro na cultura pop. A fama de Koenig em “Star Trek” foi uma bênção e uma maldição, assim como para outros integrantes do elenco como William Shatner (capitão Kirk), Leonard Nimoy (Spock), DeForest Kelley (dr. McCoy), Nichelle Nichols (Uhura), James Doohan (Scotty) e Takei, que interpretou o tenente Sulu. Eles eram frequentemente rotulados por papéis específicos por estarem tão intimamente associados a “Star Trek”. “Durante a maior parte dos anos 1970, eu não trabalhei nada, e culpei o fato de ser rotulado”, disse Koenig ao St. Petersburg Times em 1998. Mais tarde, ele conseguiu um papel fixo na série de ficção científica dos anos 1990 “Babylon 5” e atuou como autor, roteirista e, ocasionalmente, diretor. Koenig nasceu em 14 de setembro de 1936, foi criado na cidade de Nova York e estudou na Universidade da Califórnia, em Los Angeles, antes de iniciar sua carreira profissional como ator. Ele sofreu uma tragédia pessoal em 2010, quando seu filho, o ator Andrew Koenig, tirou a própria vida. Koenig casou-se com sua esposa Judy em 1965. O casal também teve uma filha, a atriz Danielle Koenig.

item.title: Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy (shoulder) out vs. Auburn
item.description: Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy will miss Saturday's game against Auburn with a shoulder injury, head coach Pete Golding confirmed Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy will miss Saturday's game against Auburn with a shoulder injury, head coach Pete Golding confirmed Monday. According to multiple reports, the junior star sustained a dislocated shoulder after a hard tackle in Saturday's 34-27 loss at Texas. He finished the game with 16 carries for 36 yards and one reception for six yards. "Obviously he's not going to play this week," Golding said Monday. "We'll evaluate that going forward ... he's still getting some MRIs. It's a different injury than he had before." The Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC), who dropped from No. 7 to No. 12 following the loss to the Longhorns, will face Auburn (4-3, 2-3) on Saturday in Oxford, Miss. Lacy has rushed for 388 yards and five touchdowns and added 10 catches for 33 yards through six games this season. He earned first-team All-American honors in 2025 after rushing for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pennsylvania measles cases rise to 1,360, state health department says
item.description: The Pennsylvania Health Department on Monday reported 1,360 measles cases in the state, up 22 cases from its previous update.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Pennsylvania Health Department on Monday reported 1,360 measles cases in the state, up 22 cases from its previous update. Here are key details: Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 258 as of October 26, according to state health department data The Pennsylvania state health department has reported [USN:L4N45M1NB TEXT:"five"] measles-related deaths so far in 2026, but the CDC has confirmed only [USN:L4N46610J TEXT:"three"] measles-associated deaths The US has recorded 4,588 measles cases this year as of October 22, according to CDC data The CDC previously [USN:L4N45Z1Q3 TEXT:"said"] it would deploy additional support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak

item.title: Presidenta encargada espera que diálogo brinde espacio a todos, incluyendo los que han hecho daño a Venezuela
item.description: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmó el lunes que espera que las negociaciones con una facción de la oposición ofrezcan un espacio para que todas las voces sean escuchadas; esto ocurre un día después de que la líder opositora María Corina Machado regresara al país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, afirmó el lunes que espera que las negociaciones con una facción de la oposición ofrezcan un espacio para que todas las voces sean escuchadas; esto ocurre un día después de que la líder opositora María Corina Machado regresara al país. "Espero que el diálogo siga brindando un espacio para la participación política, y que aquellos que han hecho daño a Venezuela —quienes pidieron sanciones y agresiones externas— sientan algo de remordimiento y arrepentimiento", declaró Rodríguez durante una visita a un hospital militar en Caracas. "Espero que tanto el diálogo como el programa para la coexistencia democrática y la paz puedan ofrecer un espacio donde todas las voces sean escuchadas; donde se puedan escuchar aquellas voces que buscan el bien del país", dijo. El regreso de Machado a Venezuela, tras varios intentos fallidos, podría tensar sus vínculos con la administración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump. Washington ha señalado que ella tiene pleno derecho a estar en Venezuela, pero, al mismo tiempo, ha elogiado a la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez y respalda un proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno de Rodríguez y grupos opositores que no incluyen al movimiento Vente Venezuela, liderado por Machado. Las conversaciones, que han continuado a lo largo de este mes, contemplan la reestructuración del Consejo Nacional Electoral y del máximo tribunal de justicia, de cara a unas eventuales elecciones.

item.title: ANÁLISIS De vuelta en Venezuela, Machado debe conciliar aspiraciones de sus seguidores y las de EEUU
item.description: María Corina Machado, quien regresó a Venezuela el domingo tras casi un año, se encuentra en una situación delicada, ya que busca impulsar las elecciones que sus seguidores reclaman pero sin entrar en conflicto con el proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno encargado y un sector más amplio de la oposición, respaldado por Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Mayela Armas, Julia Symmes Cobb
item.content:encoded: María Corina Machado, quien regresó a Venezuela el domingo tras casi un año, se encuentra en una situación delicada, ya que busca impulsar las elecciones que sus seguidores reclaman pero sin entrar en conflicto con el proceso de negociación entre el Gobierno encargado y un sector más amplio de la oposición, respaldado por Estados Unidos. El retorno de Machado, tras varios intentos fallidos, podría tensar sus vínculos con el Gobierno de Donald Trump. Sin embargo, Washington, que ha dicho que tiene pleno derecho a estar en Venezuela, también ha elogiado a la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez y ha respaldado un proceso de negociación entre su Gobierno y un sector de la oposición que excluye al movimiento político de Machado, Vente Venezuela. Las conversaciones, que siguieron este mes, consideran reestructurar el Consejo Nacional Electoral y el Tribunal Supremo de Justicia antes de unas eventuales elecciones. Ambos organismos están integrados por leales al oficialismo y además respaldaron a Nicolás Maduro —capturado en enero— en unas controvertidas elecciones presidenciales, a pesar de que los recuentos publicados por el movimiento de Machado mostraban una victoria contundente de su candidato. Los[USN:L6N46B05Q TEXT:" seguidores "]de Machado —decenas de miles de los cuales rodearon su caravana el domingo entre Barquisimeto y Caracas, ondeando banderas, coreando su nombre y entregándole rosarios— anhelan las elecciones y la consideran la próxima presidenta del país. Ella ha planteado que los comicios deberían llevarse a cabo en 2027. El equipo de Machado no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Al ser consultada sobre si Machado participaría en las negociaciones, Rodríguez dijo esperar que el diálogo brinde un espacio a quienes abogaron por sanciones contra el país, una crítica que el partido gobernante suele dirigir a la líder opositora. "Espero que tanto el diálogo como el programa para la coexistencia democrática y la paz puedan ofrecer un espacio donde todas las voces sean escuchadas; donde se puedan escuchar aquellas voces que buscan el bien del país", dijo Rodríguez. Aunque Machado ha intentado durante años cultivar una alianza con Trump, el republicano declaró el mes pasado que aún era demasiado pronto para plantear elecciones democráticas. El domingo, Trump dijo desconocer los planes de regreso de Machado, una afirmación que fue cuestionada por una persona al tanto de los movimientos de la líder venezolana. RIESGO DE "CORTOCIRCUITO" CON WASHINGTON El afán de Machado de que haya comicios podría provocar un "cortocircuito" en la relación con Estados Unidos y en el plan de tres fases —estabilización, recuperación y transición— que Washington propone para Venezuela, explicó Ricardo Ríos, director de la consultora de riesgo político Poder y Estrategia. "La idea es celebrar elecciones regionales antes de las presidenciales; es probable que ella presione para obtener garantías electorales y para que las elecciones presidenciales se lleven a cabo lo antes posible", agregó. Pero aún queda mucho por definir antes de que los votantes acudan a las urnas, señaló. "¿Qué garantías tiene el sector gobernante para dejar el poder?", planteó Ríos. "Eso es algo que todavía debe definirse para que esto sea viable; de lo contrario, por muy popular que ella sea, la situación se complica". Que Machado haya vuelto de forma segura fue el resultado directo de las negociaciones, dijo el domingo el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, añadiendo que espera que todos los actores políticos respalden las conversaciones. La Unión Europea se expresó en el mismo sentido en un comunicado emitido el lunes. Señaló que las autoridades y todos los actores políticos deberían impulsar "un diálogo inclusivo, liderado por venezolanos, hacia la celebración de elecciones libres y justas". "El recibimiento que tuvo ayer (domingo) solo reforzará la tendencia a exigir resultados inmediatos", comentó Phil Gunson, analista senior para la región andina de Crisis Group. "Esto no solo podría provocar una reacción por parte de los sectores más radicales del Gobierno, sino que -en caso de tener éxito- podría derivar en una ruptura política en lugar de una transición pacífica, con garantías postelectorales insuficientes y un país potencialmente ingobernable". El sector opositor que participa en las conversaciones, encabezado por Dinorah Figuera —legisladora elegida en 2015 en el último órgano legislativo venezolano reconocido por Estados Unidos—, calificó el regreso de Machado como un paso significativo dentro del plan estadounidense de tres fases. "Su papel también está asociado a la interpretación de las señales que Estados Unidos ha planteado de reconstrucción y reconciliación. Ella tiene que ser aliada de la negociación", señaló Oswaldo Ramírez, de ORC Consultores. "Hubo un mensaje de Rubio que fue claro (...) No la veo torpedeando la negociación. Ella no puede salirse del rayado".

item.title: New Zealand welcome back eight players but no Savea for November fixtures
item.description: New Zealand will be without injured captain Ardie Savea for their Nations Championship fixtures in November, but will welcome back eight players who had been sidelined with various ailments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand will be without injured captain Ardie Savea for their Nations Championship fixtures in November, but will welcome back eight players who had been sidelined with various ailments. • Loose forward Savea injured his shoulder in New Zealand's gruelling series loss to South Africa, with flyhalf Ruben Love another of nine players who miss out with injury • Prop Saula Ma'u and first five-eighth Josh Jacomb are two uncapped players who have been called up • Jordie Barrett, Richie Mo'unga, Anton Lienert-Brown, Quinn Tupaea, Ethan Blackadder, Anton Segner, Asafo Aumua and Fehi Fineanganofo all return from various knocks • Loose forwards Leicester Fainga'anuku and Christian Lio-Willie also make a return having been selected by coach Dave Rennie • New Zealand, who top the Southern Hemisphere pool, play Scotland, Wales and England on consecutive weekends from November 7 to complete their Nations Championship fixtures • "This is a really strong squad we have selected. It's great to officially welcome George, Saula, Leicester, Christian, Jamie and Chay back into the squad. They have all shown fantastic form," Rennie said Forwards: Ethan Blackadder, George Bell, Scott Barrett, George Bower, Ethan de Groot, Leicester Fainga'anuku, Jamie Hannah, Fabian Holland, Peter Lakai, Saula Ma'u, Fletcher Newell, Xavier Numia, Anton Segner, Codie Taylor, Pasilio Tosi, Tupou Vaa'i, Josh Lord, Christian Lio-Willie, Wallace Sititi Backs: Jordie Barrett, Beauden Barrett, Chay Fihaki, Fehi Fineanganofo, Rieko Ioane, Anton Lienert-Brown, Damian McKenzie, Richie Mo'unga, Josh Moorby, Kyle Preston, Cam Roigard, Cortez Ratima, Timoci Tavatavanawai, Quinn Tupaea, Will Jordan, Josh Jacomb

item.title: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after truce
item.description: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign". The report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel examined violations against Palestinian children since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on October 7, 2023 up to September this year. It said Israeli authorities had kept committing "genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza", and that the situation had also continued to deteriorate in the occupied West Bank. Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had [USN:L2N3V306V TEXT:"committed genocide in Gaza"] and that top Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu incited these acts — accusations that Israel called scandalous. The Israeli mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel. “The attempt to destroy the Jewish state ... continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel’s legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend itself," Ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement. HEAVY MUNITIONS HIT POPULATED AREAS, COMMISSION SAYS The commission found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire in Gaza. It said the [USN:L1N3YO0RL TEXT:""Yellow Line""] which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, was encroaching increasingly into Gaza, and becoming a de facto border, which the report said reflected Israel’s expanding territorial control of Gaza. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. In its report to the UN Security Council, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and October 6, 2023, to 254 between October 7, 2023 and September 30, 2026. Commission Chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said the intentional killing of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank formed part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians. Military operations since January 2025 have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 Palestinians remaining displaced as of August 2026, the report said. The commission also faulted the Palestinian Authority, saying it had targeted Palestinians who voice dissenting views and that journalists and human rights defenders had been killed and injured.

item.title: Derrota expressiva de Flávio Bolsonaro torna improvável anulação da eleição, dizem fontes e analistas
item.description: A magnitude da derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com o senador ficando mais de 4 milhões de votos atrás, torna improvável que seus esforços para anular a votação tenham sucesso, segundo fontes e analistas.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões, Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: A magnitude da derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com o senador ficando mais de 4 milhões de votos atrás, torna improvável que seus esforços para anular a votação tenham sucesso, segundo fontes e analistas. Flávio seguiu o exemplo de seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que está em prisão domiciliar por tentativa de golpe de Estado, ao se recusar a reconhecer a derrota para Lula, que conquistou um quarto mandato histórico. O senador questionou uma decisão tomada no final da tarde do domingo pelo ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que prorrogou a votação por duas horas devido a alegados problemas no deslocamento de eleitores. O senador afirmou que pediria a anulação da eleição. “É impossível reconhecer o resultado das eleições no contexto que as coisas aconteceram. Vamos pedir a anulação”, disse Flávio a jornalistas após o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) declarar Lula vencedor no domingo. Flávio lembrou que Zanin foi indicado por Lula para o STF. De acordo com três fontes ouvidas pela Reuters, duas do TSE e uma do STF, são remotas as chances de prosperar uma eventual tentativa de anulação das eleições de domingo por parte de Flávio, uma vez que a diferença de votos foi expressiva e o próprio presidente do TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, já descartou qualquer problema. Nunes Marques foi indicado ao STF por Jair Bolsonaro. Menos de 35 mil votos, ou cerca de 0,03% do total, foram registrados nas duas horas extras de votação determinadas pelo STF, de acordo com uma análise dos registros eleitorais feita pelo professor Pedro Burgos, do Insper. "Do ponto de vista prático considero muito pouco provável que esse pedido seja acolhido. Não diria que é impossível, mas a possibilidade é bastante remota", disse Rubens Beça, mestre e doutor em Direito Constitucional e professor da USP. "Para que a anulação fosse admitida, seria necessário demonstrar, na análise do tribunal, que a quantidade de votos potencialmente afetados pela decisão, nas seções que permaneceram abertas entre 17h e 19h, seria suficiente para alterar o resultado da eleição. Ocorre que a diferença de votos foi expressiva." A petição de Flávio também é enfraquecida pelo fato de que sua campanha também solicitou uma prorrogação da votação devido às fortes chuvas na região sul, de tendência conservadora. A Reuters procurou a defesa da campanha de Flávio no TSE para verificar se vão mesmo tentar anular a votação do segundo turno, mas não obteve resposta de imediato. A recusa do senador em reconhecer a derrota pode desencadear protestos em um país onde a confiança no sistema eleitoral e na independência judicial têm sido abalada nos últimos anos, afirmam observadores. Jair Bolsonaro mergulhou o Brasil em uma profunda crise democrática após a eleição de 2022, quando seus apoiadores invadiram as sedes dos Três Poderes em protesto contra o resultado. Posteriormente, ele foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por planejar um golpe de Estado. Enquanto Flávio se prepara para eventualmente contestar o resultado, líderes mundiais rapidamente se manifestaram para reconhecer a vitória de Lula, com mensagens de parabéns chegando da União Europeia, do México, da França, do Canadá, da Índia e da Rússia. Presidentes de direita recém-eleitos na Colômbia, no Peru e no Chile também se juntaram ao grupo de líderes que reconheceram os resultados de domingo, mas o governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, permaneceu em silêncio. (Reportagem de Oliver Griffin, Luciana Magalhães, Gabriel Araujo, Eduardo Simões e Lisandra Paraguassu, em São Paulo, e Ricardo Brito, em Brasília)

item.title: After return of opposition leader, Venezuela's acting president says hopes dialogue will offer space for all voices
item.description: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Monday that she hopes negotiations with a faction of the opposition will offer space for all voices to be heard, a day after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to the country.
item.dc:creator: Deisy Buitrago
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Monday that she hopes negotiations with a faction of the opposition will offer space for all voices to be heard, a day after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to the country. “I hope the dialogue continues to provide a space for political participation, and that those who have harmed Venezuela, those who called for sanctions and external aggression, feel some remorse and regret," the acting president said during a visit to a military hospital in Caracas. “I hope both the dialogue and the program for democratic coexistence and peace can provide a space where all voices can be heard, where voices seeking the good of the country can be heard." Machado's return to Venezuela after [USN:L1N45F02O TEXT:"several failed attempts"] risks [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"straining her ties"] with US President Donald Trump's administration. Washington has said she has every right to be in Venezuela, but has praised Rodriguez and supports a negotiation process between the Rodriguez government and opposition groups that does not include Machado's Vente Venezuela movement. The talks, which have continued this month, would remake the electoral council and top court ahead of eventual elections.

item.title: Mental health accommodations at work — what employers can ask, expect and change
item.description: Mark S. Goldstein of Reed Smith LLP offers guidance on handling mental health accommodation requests, including recognizing requests, addressing performance concerns and revisiting approved accommodations as business needs evolve.
item.dc:creator: Mark Goldstein
item.content:encoded: Recognizing requests, managing performance and revisiting approved arrangements as business needs evolve. An employee requests remote work as an accommodation for a mental health condition. Another relies on an approved schedule adjustment to manage symptoms, but the employer withdraws it when workplace requirements change. A third is offered a replacement for an existing accommodation and questions whether the alternative adequately meets their disability-related needs. Each situation calls for an individualized assessment. An employee may need an accommodation despite being able to perform the job without it. An approved arrangement may warrant reconsideration as operations change. And a proposed alternative must be evaluated for how effectively it addresses the employee's limitations. Employers have reported a substantial increase in mental health-related accommodation requests in recent years, making these decisions increasingly significant. This article examines the legal landscape and offers practical guidance for recognizing requests, addressing performance concerns and revisiting approved accommodations when business conditions change. RECOGNIZE THE REQUEST WITHOUT REQUIRING LEGAL TERMINOLOGY According to guidance from the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, an employee generally must communicate a need for a workplace change because of a medical condition. The request need not be written or use the terms "ADA" or "reasonable accommodation." A supervisor told that a schedule adjustment is needed for treatment should not wait for a formal application before referring the issue for review. Managers should recognize possible requests, not diagnose employees from behavior. The human resources department can clarify the limitation, the requested adjustment and the connection between them. A request initiates an assessment, not an automatic entitlement to the employee's preferred solution. A symptom-free day is not a disability coverage test. Under Americans with Disabilities Act regulations, an episodic impairment can qualify if it would substantially limit a major life activity when active, and beneficial effects of measures such as medication generally are disregarded when determining disability. Where the disability or accommodation need is not obvious and has not already been adequately documented, reasonable supporting documentation may be appropriate. Keep the inquiry focused on the disability and relevant limitations. An employer generally cannot demand complete medical records or keep requesting information already sufficiently provided. A useful provider inquiry connects a functional limitation to the work. For example, when a provider identifies difficulty processing competing instructions, HR can seek clarification about written priorities or scheduled check-ins. The provider supplies medical information about limitations and effectiveness, while the employer evaluates the job-specific accommodation. Possible mental health accommodations include changes to schedules or breaks, time for treatment, quiet workspaces, written instructions, leave and telework. These are options to evaluate, not automatic entitlements. The inquiry should address how an adjustment responds to this employee's limitations in this job. Keep medical information confidential and separate from ordinary personnel records. Supervisors may receive necessary work restrictions and accommodation instructions, but that does not justify distributing unrelated clinical information. A scheduling manager needs to know the approved hours, not the employee's treatment history. SEPARATE PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS FROM ACCOMMODATION NEEDS The ADA generally does not require eliminating essential functions or lowering production standards applied to employees in the same job. It may, however, require changing how work is performed so an employee can meet those standards. A request raised during performance counseling does not automatically erase warranted prior discipline. The employer should nevertheless evaluate prospective accommodation promptly, rather than treat performance management as a reason not to engage. When assessing subsequent improvement, account for whether an approved adjustment has actually been implemented. The reverse shortcut is also problematic: Satisfactory performance does not necessarily establish that an accommodation is unnecessary. In Tudor v. Whitehall Central School District (2d Cir. 2025), a teacher with post-traumatic stress disorder challenged the denial of an afternoon break after policy and scheduling changes affected earlier arrangements. The district court granted summary judgment because she acknowledged being able to perform her essential functions without the break. The Second Circuit vacated and remanded, holding that this ability did not, by itself, defeat her accommodation claim. Disability, reasonableness and undue-hardship defenses remained available. The decision does not guarantee the requested adjustment, but it cautions against assuming that an employee who keeps working has no continuing accommodation need. WHEN OPERATIONS CHANGE, DISTINGUISH REPLACEMENT FROM WITHDRAWAL Approval is not necessarily the end of the process. Consider a national employer introducing standardized schedules. An employee's approved schedule preserves time for recurring mental health treatment, but the new system would assign conflicting shifts. The company needs to evaluate the effect on that arrangement, not simply rely on the business rationale for standardization. First, identify the actual conflict. Does the schedule create an uncovered essential duty or does it merely require an exception in the new system? Reasonable accommodation can require modifying a workplace policy for an individual without abandoning the policy for everyone. Next, distinguish replacing the arrangement from declining accommodation. EEOC guidance generally permits selection among reasonable, effective alternatives, with consideration of the employee's preference. Choosing an easier or less costly effective option does not necessarily require proving that the original accommodation creates undue hardship. Bourke v. Collins (7th Cir. 2025) illustrates the distinction. Pandemic entrance restrictions disrupted parking and mobility-scooter arrangements for a Department of Veterans Affairs employee. Applying ADA liability standards under the Rehabilitation Act, the court affirmed summary judgment because the offered alternative reasonably accommodated him. It rejected a categorical requirement to prove undue hardship whenever an accommodation changes. The court also noted that, viewing the evidence in the employee's favor, the VA's initial withdrawal without consultation caused an interactive-process breakdown. That alone did not establish liability under the governing circuit law. The practical lesson is to evaluate and discuss an effective replacement, not to cancel first and investigate later. Past flexibility also requires context. In Hayes v. GStek Inc. (5th Cir. May 8, 2026), an Army contractor's information technology employee sought full-time telework for disabilities including depression and social anxiety disorder. The court affirmed judgment on the pleadings, concluding that onsite attendance was essential in that position and temporary pandemic telework had not permanently changed its essential functions. It also found a hybrid arrangement reasonable. Hayes did not involve withdrawal of previously approved full-time disability telework. It is a reminder to examine the actual duties and history, not a general rule against remote work accommodations. In the scheduling example, a different shift might preserve treatment access, but the employer should not assume appointments can move. An alternative must address the relevant limitation. If accommodation in the current job is unavailable, consideration of reassignment to a vacant position for which the employee is qualified may also be necessary. MAKE INDIVIDUALIZED DECISIONS WORKABLE AT SCALE Large employers can centralize review without predetermining the result. HR, legal and operations can establish common staffing requirements and available options. A designated team can then evaluate how those facts affect each employee's limitations and approved arrangement. Where undue hardship is asserted, the ADA regulations require consideration of significant difficulty or expense in context, including the affected facility's resources, the covered employer's overall resources and operational effects. A local budget objection does not end the inquiry. Nor does national head count make employees in specialized roles or different locations interchangeable. Record the relevant change, the options considered and the basis for the selected arrangement. Set an implementation date and a review point, rather than relying on an open-ended approval or an automatic expiration. These are practical controls, not a substitute for the applicable legal analysis. Before rollout, identify affected accommodations, assign responsibility for implementing approved exceptions and establish a way to report problems. Consider interim measures where needed and follow up on effectiveness. An approval recorded in HR's system is of little practical use if scheduling software overrides it or managers assess attendance points against the approved arrangement. Assess overlapping leave rights separately. Eligible employees of covered employers may qualify for Family and Medical Leave Act time off for mental health conditions involving inpatient care or qualifying continuing treatment. Applicable state and local laws may provide additional protections. An ADA determination does not resolve those separate obligations. FINAL THOUGHTS Mental health accommodations call for informed decisions throughout the employment relationship, not just at initial approval. Employers can preserve legitimate performance expectations and operational flexibility while recognizing continuing limitations. The objective is a reasoned, individualized decision and, where accommodation is required, an arrangement that works in practice. The author would like to thank associate Maria G. Arroyo-Poindexter for contributing to this article.

item.title: 米天然ガス大手ＥＱＴ、130億ドルで同業買収 国内最大規模に
item.description:
Sumit Saha
[２６日 ロイター] - 米天然ガス大手のＥＱＴは２６日、同業レンジ・リソーシズを１３０億ドルの...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米天然ガス大手ＥＱＴ、130億ドルで同業買収　国内最大規模に 3:15 配信

米ペンシルベニア州エリーで開催されたイベントで講演するＥＱＴのトビー・ライス最高経営責任者。2024年9月撮影。REUTERS/Hannah Beier

Sumit Saha

[２６日 ロイター] - 米天然ガス大手のＥＱＴは２６日、同業レンジ・リソーシズを１３０億ドルの株式交換方式で買収すると発表した。米天然ガス需要が拡大する中、統合により米最大規模の天然ガス生産会社となる見通し。負債を含めた統合後の企業価値は５００億ドルを超える見込みで、取引は２０２７年１─３月期に完了する見込み。

統合後の経営はＥＱＴが主導し、本社も引き続き東部ペンシルベニア州に置く。レンジから最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）ら２人が取締役に加わる。ＥＱＴの株主は統合後の会社の約７３％を、レンジ株主は残り２７％をそれぞれ保有。５年間で計約２００億ドルのフリーキャッシュフローを生むと見込まれる。

米国では、液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）の輸出増や、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連データセンターからの電力需要の増加が顕著だ。米エネルギー情報局（ＥＩＡ）によると、米国内消費量は２５年の日量９１９億立方フィートから２７年に９４３億立方フィートに増える見通し。

ＥＱＴとレンジは、いずれもアパラチア盆地にガス資源を保有する。統合によってＥＱＴの収益力が改善するほか、掘削可能な資源を拡充。電力会社やＬＮＧの輸出業者などへの供給体制を強化する。

レンジの株主は、保有１株につきＥＱＴの０．９８７株を受け取る。ロイターの試算によると、株式価値は１２８億３０００万ドル（１株当たり５４．９１ドル）と、レンジ・リソーシズの２３日の終値に対して約２０．６％のプレミアムが付く。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：武田薬のシャイアー買収5年、大型Ｍ＆Ａの難しさ示す アングル：中国発ＳＨＥＩＮ、買収主導で増収率の回復狙う アングル：欧州天然ガス在庫が過去最低水準、冬場の調達コスト高騰リスクも アングル：アルバータ州、天然ガスでデータセンター誘致　カナダ政府の環境政策と対立 コラム：世界最大の温室効果ガス排出国の中国、クリーン発電が化石燃料を逆転 最終更新: 10/27(火) 3:15 ロイター

item.title: 米マイクロソフト、約6万人対象に希望退職を募集 コスト抑制へ
item.description: [２６日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトのが全従業員の４分の１超に当たる約６万人の従業員に対し、希望退職を募集してい...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米マイクロソフト、約6万人対象に希望退職を募集　コスト抑制へ 3:12 配信

フランス・パリ近郊にある米マイクロソフトのオフィス。2025年3月撮影。REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

[２６日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトのが全従業員の４分の１超に当たる約６万人の従業員に対し、希望退職を募集していると明らかにした。同社は巨額の人工知能（ＡＩ）投資資金を賄うため、コスト抑制に取り組んでいる。

事情に詳しい関係筋が匿名を条件に語ったところによると、対象となるのは「ＡＩエクスペリエンス」、ＡＩアシスタント「コパイロット」、財務、人事、ゲーム部門「Ｘｂｏｘ」などの従業員で、マーケティング、商業部門、セキュリティーなどの部門の従業員は対象外になるという。

マイクロソフトは、今回の募集は、カナダ、インド、英国、米国の対象チームに属する、レベル７０以下の対象従業員が利用できると説明した。

エイミー・コールマン最高人事責任者は従業員向けの文書で「この募集は、将来的に社外でのキャリアを検討している対象従業員に対し、支援を受けながら今すぐ転身するための新たな選択肢を提供するものだ。また、対象となる部門にとっては、変化するニーズに合わせて人員体制を調整するための新たな手段にもなる」と記した。

マイクロソフトは他のテクノロジー大手と同様、ＡＩ向けのデータセンターや半導体に数千億ドルを投じており、その莫大なコストに見合うだけのリターンが得られるかどうか、投資家の厳しい視線が注がれている。同社は２８日の市場引け後に第1・四半期決算を発表する予定で、２０２６暦年の設備投資額を１７５０億ドルと見込んでいる。

今回の件は、ニュースサイトのビジネス・インサイダーが最初に報じていた。

同社の株価は午後の取引で約１％上昇した。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か アングル：マイクロソフト、一時撤退検討の中国市場に踏みとどまった理由 アングル：スペースＸの宇宙データセンター、ＭＳ「海中」計画中止が示す高いハードル 最終更新: 10/27(火) 3:12 ロイター

item.title: Tata Motors' takeover bid for Iveco clears 80% acceptance threshold
item.description: India's Tata Motors takeover bid for Italian truck maker Iveco has cleared the 80% acceptance threshold, reaching 87.8% on the last day of the offer, an Italian stock market filing showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Tata Motors (TATM.NS) takeover bid for Italian truck maker Iveco has cleared the 80% acceptance threshold, reaching 87.8% on the last day of the offer, an Italian stock market filing showed on Monday. The tender offer had opened on September 7 The offer price was raised to €14.40 per share, from 14.10 per share, on October 9 Tata Motors [USN:L8N3TR2BQ TEXT:"agreed last year"] to buy Iveco's commercial vehicle business in a deal valued at €3.8 billion

item.title: Votação de Flávio Bolsonaro cresceu no 2º turno em SC
item.description: O candidato derrotado à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aumentou sua votação em Santa Catarina no segundo turno das eleições, disputado neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: O candidato derrotado à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) aumentou sua votação em Santa Catarina no segundo turno das eleições, disputado neste domingo, ao contrário do que afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) foi reeleito. Estes são os principais detalhes: “Flávio perde 5,7% e Lula ganha 14% em Santa Catarina. Os números não batem nem a pau!”, dizem posts no Facebook e no Instagram. Dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), porém, apontam que os dois candidatos aumentaram sua votação no Estado. Segundo o TSE, Flávio recebeu 66,65% dos votos válidos (3 milhões) em Santa Catarina no primeiro turno. No segundo, ele teve 69,42% (3,22 milhões). Já Lula alcançou 25,04% dos votos válidos catarinenses no primeiro turno (1,13 milhão). No segundo, o presidente teve 30,58% (1,42 milhão). O PL elegeu o governador, 2 senadores e 7 dos 16 deputados federais do Estado, além de 16 dos 40 deputados estaduais. O PT catarinense conseguiu apenas duas vagas na Câmara dos Deputados e 5 na Assembleia Legislativa. Veredicto: Falso. Tanto Flávio quanto Lula ganharam votos entre o primeiro e o segundo turnos em Santa Catarina. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: AI capital race sprints into winnowing phase
item.description: Anthropic and Meta are tapping equity markets for up to $195 bln, a third of last year's total issuance. SpaceX also struck a $40 bln chip deal. Giants can lean on their fundraising edge as tighter credit and slipping stocks stymie upstarts. The cost to do so, however, is rising.
item.dc:creator: Karen Kwok
item.content:encoded: Even by the crazed standards of the artificial intelligence boom, $235 billion is a lot of money to earmark in a single day. SpaceX unveiled a $40 billion chip-leasing deal on Monday, Meta Platforms [USN:L3N46C0RK TEXT:"laid out"] plans to raise up to $95 billion of equity and Anthropic released the prospectus for an initial public offering that [USN:L4N42G1FB TEXT:"could fetch"] another $100 billion. Even as credit markets tighten and stocks slip, giants are pushing their fundraising advantage ever harder. The catch is the rising price. So-called neoclouds like CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which borrow heavily to build servers for AI developers, have experienced [USN:L6N46113K TEXT:"dramatic"] sell-offs in their shares and debt. Yet SpaceX (SPCX.O) , effectively a turbo-charged neocloud, sealed what is the largest-ever financing for GPUs, the most popular chips for crunching chatbot calculations. Meanwhile, Anthropic's and Meta’s plans would equate to roughly one-third of last year's worldwide equity issuance, according to LSEG data. None of this comes cheap. SpaceX, Elon Musk's sprawling satellites-to-social-media conglomerate, has agreed to lease chips acquired by an Apollo Global Management-run (APO.N) vehicle. Its rent formula returns the full financed cost over 20 quarters, plus a fixed rate, meaning the investment shop led by Marc Rowan bears no risk related to the value of the silicon after a five-year lease ends. Although terms are undisclosed, lenders expect to price the deal at interest rates of 7.75% to 8.3%, Semafor reported . The ICE BofA BBB yield index, which reflects companies with a comparable credit rating to SpaceX, has an effective yield of about 6%. At least Musk's enterprise carries an investment-grade rating, meaning it can raise more cash than CoreWeave on the strength of its own finances. SpaceX is also in a stronger position than the leading AI lab. Anthropic, whose credit rating is pending, offered buyout firm Blackstone (BX.N) a yield of more than 10% on junior debt backed by chip lease payments, the Financial Times reported this month. Equity may well get squeezed, too. Meta shares are down 9% since its stock-issuance plans became clear on Wednesday. ChatGPT maker OpenAI has lowered its valuation expectations from a previously mulled $1.5 trillion to a still-frothy $1.25 trillion in discussions over a new funding round, CNBC reported . At base is a vast spending spree. AI capital expenditure could reach $7.6 trillion between 2026 and 2031, for which tech giants like Meta, Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) may issue $420 billion of debt in 2027 alone, Goldman Sachs analysts estimate . The ability to do so should prove a decisive leg-up over smaller rivals. It does nothing, however, to prove the fundamental investment case for AI, even as markets signal exhaustion. The way to bridge the gap: pay more. Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X . Anthropic on October 26 unveiled its prospectus for an initial public offering that could value the artificial intelligence lab at as much as $2 trillion, Reuters previously reported. Meta Platforms said on the same day that it intends to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising. The Facebook and Instagram owner has initiated public offerings for about $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and filed for a separate at-the-market program to sell non-voting shares worth as much as $60 billion. SpaceX said separately that an affiliate of investment firm Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the billionaire Elon Musk's rockets-to-AI company, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Average price of gasoline during Trump's term now exceeds Biden's, as midterms loom
item.description: Americans have paid more for their gasoline and diesel at the pump on average during President Donald Trump's second term than they did under his Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, according to the AAA.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Americans have paid more for their gasoline and diesel at the pump on average during President Donald Trump's second term than they did under his Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, according to the AAA. Surging fuel prices are a major thorn in Trump's side as [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] loom and the Republican Party looks to defend narrow majorities in both legislative chambers on November 3. The price of a gallon of regular gasoline has averaged $3.472 a gallon since Trump took office almost two years ago, edging out the $3.471-per-gallon average for Biden's term, according to data from the AAA. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Prices for diesel, the fuel that powers the global economy from agriculture and heavy industry to shipping, have also surpassed Biden's national average under Trump, at $4.343 a gallon compared with $4.078 a gallon. US diesel hit a record high on September 22 at $6.523 a gallon as wars in Ukraine and Iran disrupt global fuel supplies. Trump's approval rating fell to a record low this month as Americans worried about high gasoline prices, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published on October 19. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Just 23% of adults polled nationwide approve of his handling of the economy.

item.title: Actor Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' plucky Chekov, dies at 90
item.description: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90. "My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who starred alongside Koenig in the show and was a long-time friend, wrote on Facebook on Monday. Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles, the AP reported, citing his talent agent. "Star Trek" creator Gene Roddenberry picked Koenig, who had played only a few prior roles on television, when he decided to add a Russian character to the crew of the fictional Starship Enterprise. The introduction of a Russian officer who worked harmoniously with a racially and culturally diverse crew came amid the real-world Cold War tensions of the era. "We were stating tacitly that peoples of all races and creeds, nationalities could not only co-exist but care for each other deeply, and in doing so we were heralding a future that was very optimistic," Koenig once told a BBC interviewer. While Koenig was the son of Russian Jewish immigrants, he used an inauthentic Russian accent that was sometimes played for laughs. The original TV series ran for three seasons, from 1966 to 1969. Koenig appeared on 36 episodes, and then in seven movies from 1979 to 1994. "I was informed while I was still there at my audition that I had the role," Koenig told the Joplin Globe in 2008. "It seemed like an engagement that might work out over several episodes, but I had no idea that it would totally shape my career and my life." The show remained popular in syndicated reruns and inspired several later TV series and a succession of films. It attracted a devoted worldwide fan base and earned an enduring place in pop culture. Koenig's "Star Trek" fame was a blessing and a curse, as it was for cast mates such as William Shatner (Captain Kirk), Leonard Nimoy (Spock), DeForest Kelley (Dr. McCoy), Nichelle Nichols (Uhura), James Doohan (Scotty) and Takei, who played Lieutenant Sulu. They were often typecast because they were so closely associated with "Star Trek." "Most of the '70s, I didn't work at all, and I blamed it on typecasting," Koenig told the St. Petersburg Times in 1998. He later landed a regular role on the 1990s sci-fi series "Babylon 5" and was an author, script writer and occasional director. Koenig was born on September 14, 1936, raised in New York City and attended the University of California, Los Angeles, before beginning his professional acting career. He suffered a personal tragedy in 2010 when his son, actor Andrew Koenig, took his own life. Koenig married his wife Judy in 1965. They also had a daughter, actress Danielle Koenig.

item.title: Bovespa se desploma más de un 15% en jornada después de una suspensión tras reelección de Lula
item.description: El referencial bursátil brasileño Bovespa se desplomaba el lunes, y la B3 activó el mecanismo denominado "cortocircuito" en los primeros minutos de la sesión bursátil, tras la reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva el día anterior, que contrarió las expectativas del mercado y suscitó preocupación sobre la situación fiscal del país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El referencial bursátil brasileño Bovespa se desplomaba el lunes, y la B3 activó el mecanismo denominado "cortocircuito" en los primeros minutos de la sesión bursátil, tras la reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva el día anterior, que contrarió las expectativas del mercado y suscitó preocupación sobre la situación fiscal del país. Hacias las 1400 GMT, el Bovespa (.BVSP) se hundía un 15,9%, a 172.479,84 puntos. En su mínimo, llegó a los 169.516,43 puntos, con las acciones sensibles a las tasas de interés entre las que más caían, como C&A (CEAB3.SA) , que veía un desplome del 50%. B3 activó el "cortocircuito" al inicio de la sesión, suspendiendo durante 30 minutos la negociación de activos al contado, renta fija privada y opciones con acciones como activos subyacentes.
