item.title: スペースＸ、ＡＩ半導体でアポロ関連会社とリース契約 約400億ドル規模
item.description: [２６日 ロイター] - 米宇宙関連企業スペースＸは２６日、資産運用会社アポロ・グローバル・マネジメントの関連会社が...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
スペースＸ、ＡＩ半導体でアポロ関連会社とリース契約　約400億ドル規模 10/26 22:47 配信

スペースｘのロゴ。６月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[２６日 ロイター] - 米宇宙関連企業スペースＸは２６日、資産運用会社アポロ・グローバル・マネジメントの関連会社が人工知能（ＡＩ）向け半導体とサーバー機器を購入し、同社にリースする契約を締結したと明らかにした。同取引の元本総額は約４００億ドルに上る。

規制当局への提出書類によると、各リース契約は機器が到着した日から５年強の期間となる。

今回の契約は、月や火星などへの飛行を目指す野心的な計画の資金を賄うために、急増する計算能力への需要の取り込みを図るスペースＸの巨額の支出を浮き彫りにしている。

同社は年内の契約締結を目指しており、リースは半導体が納入され次第、２０２７年上期に開始される見通しだ。

同社のイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２５日、Ｘへの投稿で、画像処理装置（ＧＰＵ）の購入に向けた４００億ドルの債務による資金調達を完了したと説明。これは主に（２７年）第１・四半期および第２・四半期に納入されるＧＰＵの購入に向けた早期償還可能な債務であり、この四半期（２６年第４・四半期）に大きな影響を与えるものではないと述べていた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：ＮＡＳＡローマン宇宙望遠鏡打ち上げへ、ダークエネルギーやダークマターの解明期待 アングル：米金融大手、第2四半期は軒並み好決算　投資銀・取引部門がけん引 アングル：スペースＸ株が公開価格割れ、投資家の信頼守れるか　他案件に影響も アングル：米国で新たに44万人の「ＡＩ長者」、高級品の支出と嗜好にも変化 焦点：ラッセル指数銘柄入れ替えで26日は米株取引急増か、スペースＸなど注目 最終更新: 10/26(月) 22:47 ロイター

item.title: アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大
item.description:
Manya Saini Echo Wang
［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク ２６日 ロイター］ - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大 10/26 22:30 配信

１０月１９日撮影　REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク　２６日　ロイター］　 - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックは２６日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）申請書類を公開した。書類では巨額の赤字と急速な売上高の伸びが明らかになり、開発に多額の費用がかかる中でも、世界経済を変革し得るＡＩシステムの構築を目指す姿勢を示した。

目論見書は、過去１年間の同社の急成長を浮き彫りにした。成長を支えたのは大手テクノロジー企業による急激な支出拡大で、ＡＩ関連株の上昇を促す一方、割高な株価評価や債務増加への懸念も招いている。

アンソロピックの上場は、投資家のＡＩへの意欲を測る重要な試金石になりそうだ。投資家は、巨額投資のリターンに対する精査を強め、過度に高い企業価値の持続性に疑問を投げかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査・上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）提供会社ルネサンス・キャピタルのシニアストラテジスト、マット・ケネディ氏は「アンソロピックは、夏場よりはるかに厳しいＩＰＯ市場に臨んでいる。数カ月前、投資家は今のように企業価値を疑問視してはいなかった」と述べた。

アナリストは、債務に支えられたＡＩ投資ブームへの投資家の不安が株式・債券市場を動揺させる中、ＡＩ業界の企業価値評価は調整されるとみている。借り入れコストの上昇や債券利回りの上昇も、投資家の慎重姿勢に拍車をかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査会社ＩＰＯＸのリサーチアソシエイト、ルーカス・ミュールバウアー氏は「アンソロピックのＩＰＯは、ＡＩの主要研究機関を評価する際の基準を確立し、今後の上場案件や、ＡＩインフラ構築に資金を供給する企業への信頼に影響を与えるだろう」と指摘した。一方で、「その成功が、必ずしも全てのＡＩ事業に等しく恩恵をもたらすわけではない」と慎重な見方も示した。

アンソロピックの２０２６年上期の純損失は８０７億ドルと大幅に拡大した。主に、転換社債の公正価値が上昇したことが響いた。同期の売上高は約１６３億ドルだった。６月３０日までの３カ月間の売上高は、前年同期比１３６８％増と急増した。

市場の変動を受けて複数の企業が上場を延期する中でも、アンソロピックは上場計画を進めている。高度なモデルの開発・運用にはコンピューティングインフラへの巨額投資が必要で、ＩＰＯは多額の費用を伴うＡＩ構想の実現に向け、潤沢な資金を調達する機会となる。

＜ＡＩの可能性と危険性の両立＞

今回の申請書類では、業績や成長動向、ＩＰＯ計画など、公開前に内容の一部を伝えたロイターの一連の独自報道が確認された。

ロイターは、アンソロピックが最近の投資家向けイベントで財務情報の一部を開示した後、既存株主や出資を検討する投資家の一部が同社の評価額を約１兆５０００億ドルと見積もっていると報じていた。１週間前の約２兆ドルから低下した。

同社は目論見書で「われわれの成功は、最先端で最も高性能なＡＩモデルを開発し続ける能力に大きく依存しており、それができなければ事業に悪影響が及ぶ可能性がある」と記した。

今回のＩＰＯは、アンソロピック自身の研究が高度なＡＩシステムへの懸念を提起する中で行われる。管理された条件下での試験では、コードの破壊工作や詐欺行為の支援、情報操作といった行動が確認された。

こうした研究結果は、企業が商用化を競う中、ますます強力になるＡＩシステムをどう制御し続けるかという懸念を強めている。

目論見書では、同社のＡＩモデルが「自己保全的な行動」を示す可能性があるとし、「停止に抵抗する」試みや「情報を隠ぺい・操作する」試み、「恐喝に似た」行動などのリスクを挙げた。

アンソロピックはＩＰＯ完了後、ナスダックに銘柄コード「ＡＮＴ」で上場する。売り出す株式数や仮条件の価格帯など、募集条件は明らかにしなかった。

＜売上高が急拡大＞

研究者チームが２０２１年に設立したアンソロピックは、今年５月の資金調達で９６５０億ドルの評価額を付けた。この資金調達には、シリコンバレーや米金融界の有力企業が参加した。

アンソロピックは目論見書で「ＡＩがこれほど豊富に利用できるようになれば、工業化や電力、半導体、インターネットの影響を上回る形で、世界経済のあらゆる分野が急速に変革されると考えている」と記した。計算資源とインフラにかかる費用が金額ベースで増加し、当面は営業費用の中で最大の項目であり続けると見込んでいる。

また、売上高と売掛金が限られた数の顧客や販売経路に集中していると説明した。

アンソロピックは、最先端のＡＩシステム構築を巡り、オープンＡＩと激しい主導権争いを続けている。オープンＡＩは６月に非公開でＩＰＯを申請しており、２０２７年初めまでに上場すると見込まれている。オープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯは９月、ＡＩの安全性への懸念を理由に２６年中は上場しないと述べた。２０３０年までにＡＩが人類を絶滅させるリスクは、たとえ１０％でも「容認できない」とした。

今回のＩＰＯを引き受ける米金融機関の幹事団は、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが主導する。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 最終更新: 10/27(火) 0:59 ロイター

item.title: Anthropic's IPO: A close look at AI frontrunner's rapid growth, spiraling costs
item.description: Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Sophia
item.content:encoded: Anthropic [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"unveiled"] its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending. The company had submitted a [USN:L4N4291D9 TEXT:"confidential filing"] in June. In the recent weeks, exclusive reporting from Reuters highlighted its [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:"sweeping AI ambitions"], [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"mounting costs"] and concerns about the "[USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"existential risks to humanity"]" that advanced AI poses. Here are a few details on Anthropic's financials, business structure, and where it stands in the global AI race: BACKGROUND AND FINANCES Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic is the startup behind the Claude family of AI models. Across four tiers - Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku - Claude powers products such as Anthropic's chatbot, coding agent and the enterprise-focused Claude Cowork AI agent. Anthropic's early focus on training its models for coding tasks propelled the company to the forefront of the AI race and helped it draw a steady stream of enterprise customers. A majority of its revenue comes from businesses paying for its models per use, measured in "tokens" of information processed, in what Anthropic calls "consumption-based" revenue. It also generates revenue from its paid customer subscription tiers such as "Pro" and "Max". That has helped Anthropic grow its revenue to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year ago and $41 million in 2023. For the six months ended June 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $16.29 billion, a massive increase from $1.16 billion for the same period in 2025. The company's operating losses have ballooned over the past years. But for the first half of 2026, they stood at $693 million, narrowing from $2.14 billion in the first half of 2025, as a fourteen-fold jump in revenue offset a fivefold increase in overall expenses. COSTS, COMPUTE DEMAND AND CIRCULAR AI INVESTMENTS Computing power is Anthropic's biggest expense. The company's costs include computing fees paid to cloud services providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, costs tied to data center facilities and renting data center capacity, equipment leases and energy bills. Over the past three years, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure expenses have dwarfed its revenue. The company has committed more than [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"$600 billion"] in spending with about eight partners over a decade - one of the largest AI buildout commitments on record. Anthropic said many portions of its agreements are non-cancelable or require payments regardless of usage. It has committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon (AMZN.O) , about $114.5 billion with Google (GOOGL.O) and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years. But some of those companies are also its largest backers. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic's top shareholders, marking yet another example of the circular financing structures that have dominated capital flows in the AI industry. Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and has agreed to invest up to $20 billion more. Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic. GOVERNANCE AND STRUCTURE Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, or PBC, meaning it is legally obligated to balance profitability goals for investors with developing AI for the benefit of humanity. An independent body elects a majority of its board. The company, helmed by Dario Amodei as CEO and his sister Daniela, as president and chair of the board, will continue to operate as a PBC after its listing. It expects to keep its founders and an independent trust in control, in a structure that could limit investor oversight and public shareholders' influence. The company has said it needs to concentrate control and capital in fewer hands to reduce AI's risks. Under this arrangement, a majority vote of its seven co-founders will direct a single share of Class F stock that amounts to 50.1% of the total voting power over key corporate matters, including the election of some board directors and other matters submitted to investors. COMPETITION Anthropic's most direct competitor is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, whose 2022 launch kick-started the global race to adopt and advance AI technologies. Following Anthropic's lead in the enterprise market, OpenAI has sharpened its focus on products for developers and business customers. Anthropic is also locked in a race with Elon Musk's SpaceX, Alphabet's Google and Meta (META.O) . All of them are spending billions of dollars into model development, data centers and specialized AI chips as they vie for dominance in generative AI. Ramp data, which captures a slice of AI spending by business customers, showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1% of AI token spending in the week ended October 11.

item.title: ヨルダン教会襲撃で3人逮捕、他の組織との関連確認されず
item.description:
AbdelHadi Ramahi Eman Abouhassira Nayera Abdallah
[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] - ヨルダンの治安当局は２６日、９人が死亡した教会襲撃事件に関与した疑いで、銃撃戦の末に兄弟２人と義理の兄弟１人を逮捕した。政府高官が明らかにした。容疑者らと他の組織とのつながりはないとみられ、独自に行動したとの見方を示した。

この事件は２３日、首都アンマンの南西約１２０キロにあるカラク県ハムード村のギリシャ正教会で葬儀中に発生し、ほかにも４０人が負傷した。目撃者によると、銃撃は数分間続いたという。

公安当局はカラクの廃屋に潜伏していた容疑者を発見したと説明。投降を拒否して治安部隊を攻撃したため、部隊が応戦し、３人全員を負傷させた上で逮捕した。

治安部隊側に負傷者はでなかった。容疑者らが所持していた複数の銃器や弾薬が見つかったという。

ファラヤ内相と公安総局のアブドラ・マアイタ少将は記者会見で、過激派によるテロを容認しないと表明。ファラヤ氏は「事件はまだ解決しておらず、捜査は続いている。現時点で、彼らと他の組織とのつながりを示すものはない」と述べた。

容疑者の氏名を公表せず、イスラム過激派組織との関係の有無についても明らかにしなかった。

中東で比較的安定しているヨルダンでは、こうした暴力事件は極めて異例だ。

item.title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: Parliament authorised Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Monday to take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself — a move that could push Cairo more directly into the conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Parliament authorised Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Monday to take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself — a move that could push Cairo more directly into the conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis. Sisi had [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"asked parliament"] to approve military support for Egypt's Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requested help in fighting the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — southern gateway to the Red Sea and Egypt's Suez Canal. At least two-thirds of the chamber backed the measure, according to an official parliamentary statement. Parliament voted in closed session without publishing the tally, and no formal Saudi request for Egyptian troops has been announced. The statement did not specify what kind of support Egypt would provide. Taher al-Khouly, deputy head of parliament’s legislative committee, told Reuters that Egypt would send forces to Saudi Arabia in coordination between the two countries and at Saudi Arabia’s request. Several opposition groups opposed or declined to back the move. The Civil Democratic Movement, a coalition of opposition parties, rejected Egyptian military involvement in a regional war and said last week that Cairo’s role should focus on mediation. The Egyptian Social Democratic Party had said its lawmakers would abstain, citing a lack of information on the mission’s aims, duration and cost, while saying it remained supportive of Saudi Arabia. Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries, but it has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Mecca [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"mutual defence"] pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"signed in August"]. Ministers from the pact’s member countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"earlier this month"] and agreed to ensure the “rapid deployment” of forces and military capabilities in Saudi Arabia. Pakistan approved the agreement last week, whileTurkey's parliament began ratifying it [USN:L6N4660OA TEXT:"last week"]. Top officials from the three Mecca pact countries were meeting Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday in [USN:L2N46C041 TEXT:"a push to de-escalate the conflict"]. Britain said [USN:SPN46200R TEXT:"last week"] it would deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks. SISI SPELLS OUT LIMITS OF EGYPTIAN SUPPORT FOR SAUDIS The Cairo parliament had postponed the vote last week as Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said afterwards that Cairo advocated exploring [USN:L1N4680Z9 TEXT:""every opportunity""] to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically. Essam Farid, the speaker of the Senate, said Egypt’s position was "purely defensive" and aimed at defending Saudi territory, borders, sovereignty and holy sites against external attack. He said that it would not extend to an attack on Yemen and that Egypt stands with its brothers as "a shield that protects, not a sword that attacks". Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war, in March 2015. At that time it acted mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role. Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War. Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of Yemen's Houthi-run House of Representatives, last week urged the Cairo parliament to reject the proposal, saying Egypt would be threatening its own national security and internal stability. The Senate speaker told the chamber he had received a letter from Ahmed Obeid bin Daghr, head of Yemen’s Shura Council, which is aligned with the internationally recognised government, backing Egypt’s participation in defending Saudi Arabia. Bin Daghr said the position reflected the will of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, according to the speaker. Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . The Houthis have attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil company [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. The Saudi crown prince had sought military help from the US, but President Donald Trump did not agree to strikes on the Houthis, people familiar with the matter told Reuters in September. Washington told Riyadh that it would help with intelligence sharing and targeting, they added. (This story has been corrected to change the attribution of the remarks to Sisi, not the letter, in paragraph 13.)

item.title: Surgery Partners to be taken private by Bon Secours affiliate in $5.7 billion deal
item.description: Surgery Partners said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: Surgery Partners (SGRY.O) said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%. Private equity group Bain Capital, which has been a minority shareholder since 2017 and owns 39% of Surgery Partners, will back the deal and retain a major ownership stake after closing, the companies said. The remaining shareholders will receive $23.50 per share, implying a premium of 49% to the stock's last close. The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, highlights a growing push into outpatient surgery by healthcare operators, with not-for-profit health system Ascension having purchased surgical firm AmSurg for $3.9 billion earlier this year. The addition of Surgery Partners will expand Bon Secours Mercy Health's US footprint well beyond its more than 45 hospitals, according to the hospital system, adding over 200 sites across 30 states and about 5,000 affiliated physicians. The deal also ends a two-year strategic review during which Surgery Partners drew interest from potential buyers including Bain Capital, [USN:L4N3SK0YE TEXT:"whose bid to"] take the company private last year was rebuffed. Surgery Partners operates outpatient surgery centers, short-stay hospitals and related healthcare services across the US. "From a strategic perspective, there is some market overlap in Ohio and Kentucky, but the potential transaction would substantially broaden the system's (Bon Secours Mercy Health) national footprint, so we do not expect meaningful FTC antitrust risk issues," said Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes. Hynes said Bain retaining its ownership position under the proposed transaction is expected to help the deal close. In 2025, Surgery Partners generated $3.31 billion in revenue and reported an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share.

item.title: Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job". "US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again," Netanyahu said in a televised appearance late on Sunday night. "He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me." In his own social media post on Sunday, Trump, who launched the Iran war jointly with Netanyahu in February, said: "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!" Netanyahu said Trump was willing to take action "that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat", but only as long as Netanyahu himself remains in power. "And I have already instructed the Mossad and the IDF (military) to bring down this regime, to bring down this regime because that is the only way to put an end to this threat," Netanyahu said, referring to Israel's main intelligence service and military. Asked for comment on Netanyahu's remarks, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said: “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait." "The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]," Kelly added via email, referring to the November 3 vote in the US. Trump first endorsed Netanyahu on October 18, reiterating his support in a post on Truth Social on Sunday. Asked by reporters later on Monday whether Netanyahu had requested the second endorsement, Trump said: "I never spoke about it." "I put out both endorsements. I put out both... I think he's done a very good job as prime minister under very trying conditions." Netanyahu's leading opponent, centrist former military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, posted his own comments on social media, praising Trump as "a true friend of Israel". "I value his efforts and his commitment to Israel’s security, and I am confident that he will work in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people." EISENKOT ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF FEAR-MONGERING Tuesday's vote, Israel's first since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, is the first chance for voters to deliver a [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"verdict on the worst security failure"] in generations and the wars on multiple fronts that followed. With Netanyahu already at the helm of the most right-wing government in Israeli history, politics have shifted even further to the right. Nearly all Jewish-led parties, including that of the hawkish Eisenkot, now [USN:L6N4660BW TEXT:"oppose the "two-state solution" that underpinned decades of peace negotiations"] with the Palestinians. But many voters say the divisive politics of Israel's longest-serving leader make the country weaker. Polls suggest Netanyahu's Likud Party will lose seats, potentially depriving his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties of its narrow majority. Eisenkot and an array of opposition parties ranging from the rump of the centre-left to the right, also have no clear path to unseat him. Netanyahu, 77, is an unrivaled master of political survival: the only time since 2009 that opponents managed to wrest him briefly from the premiership, it took four inconclusive elections within two years to get him out. He was back 18 months later. Neither side planned major public events for Monday. But both posted on social media, drumming on the election's major themes — for Netanyahu, that he is the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's enemies; for his opponents, that his divisive politics have weakened the country. Netanyahu shared an AI-generated video on Monday of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father Ali Khamenei was killed on the first night of US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Lying in a hospital bed, the younger Khamenei says his own vote would be "definitely not Bibi. Another term like this and I will be meeting my father sooner than expected." On Sunday Netanyahu posted a computer-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv, saying Israel was in existential danger from Iran. [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot responded"] by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats—including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv. This time, it won’t work for him." Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu carries its own political risks a week before a legislative election in which his own Republicans are seeking to hold onto power. The Iran war is deeply unpopular in the United States, blamed for a surge in prices especially for fuel. Major fighting has been suspended for months after ceasefire negotiations held without Israeli participation.

item.title: Anthropic's soaring sales, steep losses put AI frenzy to IPO test
item.description: Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight. AI has captured investors' imagination with the promise of a technological leap that could transform businesses, accelerate scientific breakthroughs and unlock vast productivity gains. That has fueled enormous investments in computing infrastructure and AI development, while also stoking skepticism over the scale and pace of the spending. Anthropic's listing comes at a critical time for global markets as investors closely assess whether the billions of dollars being poured into the technology will generate returns to justify sky-high valuations. "There is still enormous excitement about AI's potential to transform businesses, turbocharge productivity and reshape entire industries, but investors are becoming more discerning," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club. Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"widened sharply"] to $80.7 billion, largely due to a non-operating item related to bonds convertible into the company's shares. Despite the huge expenses, its operating loss for the same period narrowed to $693 million and its adjusted operating income swung to a positive $1.62 billion compared with a loss of $1.85 billion a year ago. The company, which is expected to go public before Thanksgiving, said its revenue grew a staggering 1,368% in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but it warned in the prospectus that its revenue growth rate could decline and fluctuate from time to time. The filing [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"confirmed a series of Reuters "][USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"exclusives"] that offered an early peek at its contents before Anthropic made it public, including details of its financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans. Its prospectus details the risks from the powerful technology, from potential misuse and security threats to concerns that advanced systems could produce outputs that "could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative", including behavior resembling blackmail. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei [USN:L1N45403P TEXT:"has called for a slowdown"] in the development of AI. VALUATION EXPECTATIONS Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"recent investor event"]. "The offering is for the faithful, that sooner or later, they're going to get some return on that invested capital," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital. Anthropic's IPO [USN:L6N46216E TEXT:"currently stands alone"] in what was once expected to be a crowded fall listing market. Analysts [USN:L6N46C0UF TEXT:"said"] that would give it access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions. "Anthropic's IPO will establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure build-out," IPOX research associate Lukas Muehlbauer said. Analysts expect valuations of the AI sector to correct as [USN:L6N4611C1 TEXT:"investor unease"] with the debt-fueled AI investment boom roils equity and debt markets. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have also added to investor caution. "Anthropic is entering an IPO market that is far more challenging than the summer. Investors were not questioning valuations the same way a few months ago," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs. BALANCING AI'S PROMISES AND PERILS Anthropic said more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30% of Global 2000 firms were its customers that generated at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30. The IPO comes as Anthropic's own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviors including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation. "Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures," the prospectus said. The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud services providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical infrastructure parts. These relationships can create "dependencies and potential vulnerabilities", it said. Anthropic, which [USN:L4N41X0QE TEXT:"did not reveal"] the terms of its offering, will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" after the [USN:L4N469189 TEXT:"IPO closes"]. SCORCHING PACE OF GROWTH Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers who left OpenAI after disagreements over governance and AI safety, was [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"valued at $965 billion"] in a funding round in May. It remains locked in a fierce battle with OpenAI to lead the race to build the most advanced AI systems. The company named Netflix's billionaire co-founder Reed Hastings as its lead independent director. In keeping with Nasdaq rules, Anthropic identified itself as a "controlled company" based on the power of its Long-Term Benefit Trust to elect a majority of its board. The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to rise in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense. Anthropic has committed more than $600 billion to computing deals with partners including Amazon and Google, ranking among the largest AI infrastructure commitments on record. Anthropic's IPO follows that of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which rewrote the IPO record books in June, when it [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] a $75 billion offering that valued the company at $1.75 trillion. Goldman Sachs secured the prestigious lead-left role on Anthropic's IPO, working alongside Morgan Stanley, which is also a lead underwriter. Both banks declined to comment. Twenty other banks were named as underwriters with Morgan Stanley serving as stabilization agent, overseeing the stock's early trading. The IPO mandates mark another win for the two banks, which also held lead roles in SpaceX's IPO.

item.title: Cadence unveils suite of AI models that chipmakers can run in-house
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 26 : Cadence Design Systems on Monday launched a portfolio of AI models tuned to help design computer chips, deepening its open-source model work with Nvidia and diverging from rival Synopsys' recent deal with OpenAI.Both companies make software used to design computing chips — a process
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 26 : Cadence Design Systems on Monday launched a portfolio of AI models tuned to help design computer chips, deepening its open-source model work with Nvidia and diverging from rival Synopsys' recent deal with OpenAI. Both companies make software used to design computing chips — a process that involves arranging billions of transistors precisely to meet cost and performance targets — and are racing to have AI "agents" use those tools on behalf of human engineers to speed up the process. The new suite, called Cadence Maestro, introduced on Monday, was built in part on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron model and secured with Nvidia's OpenShell safety technology, the companies said. Cadence said customers can run the models on its own cloud or any public cloud, or keep them entirely in-house behind their own firewalls and data centers.

Shares of Cadence, which reports earnings after market close on Monday, rose 3.9 per cent after the announcement. Customers can also fine-tune the models on their own chip designs, and early results show up to 30 per cent higher quality and up to five times better cost-efficiency than general-purpose models, it added. The Cadence approach contrasts with that of its largest competitor, Synopsys, which on September 30 said it would develop an AI model with OpenAI and share revenue with the ChatGPT maker. That model, GPT-Synopsys, will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure. Paul Cunningham, a Cadence senior vice president, framed Maestro as model-agnostic, saying, "there are more (AI) model providers out there than there are (chip design software) vendors." When asked whether Cadence might strike its own deals with proprietary AI labs, Cunningham said both open- and closed-weight approaches were being "pursued equally," and that working with commercial labs was "part of the Maestro vision," though he declined to elaborate. The first Maestro models will reach select early-access customers in the fourth quarter, Cadence said.

BRUSSELS, Oct 26 : The European Commission said on Monday it had accepted Chinese online retail platform Temu's action plan to remedy a breach of the EU's Digital Services Act, following a fine imposed on the company in May. The plan focuses on five measures to remedy the breach, and Temu now has four months to conduct an interim risk assessment, the Commission, which acts as EU regulator, said in a statement. The Commission had imposed a €200 million ($224.08 million) fine on Temu in May for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal products. A spokesperson for Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it welcomed the Commission's approval of its plan under which the company will have to assess possible shortcomings of its content moderation system, among other steps. Temu, along with Shein and other ecommerce platforms, has been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value ecommerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free. ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: Brazil's Lula hangs on, but his final term promises to be toughest yet
item.description: Congress has amassed significant power over government spending in the past decade, which could frustrate Lula's promises to maintain his signature welfare programs.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle
item.content:encoded: Brazil's octogenarian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva faces an uphill battle from day one of his final term, analysts say, with his plans hemmed in by economic headwinds and a right-wing Congress. Already the country's oldest president, Lula overcame a first-round loss to pull off a [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"surprise runoff victory"] against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday, securing 51.8% of votes and a record fourth term just two days before his 81st birthday. He will take office on January 5 after winning what he has said was his last election, hanging on to power in a country that has swung dramatically to the right since his first electoral victory in 2002. FISCAL POLICY 'HIS BIGGEST CHALLENGE' "Lula has shown that he still is the dominant political figure of his era, but he is weaker," Michael Ahn Paarlberg of the Center for International Policy think tank said. Brazil's incoming Congress is its [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"most conservative"] since the country's return to democracy in the 1980s, with Bolsonaro's party and its allies enjoying majorities in both chambers. "He's likely to be a lame duck from the start," said Oliver Stuenkel, an international relations professor at Sao Paulo's Getulio Vargas Foundation, who predicted Lula would struggle to build a coalition to pass much of his agenda. As of Monday morning, Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, had yet to concede, and Lula faced the prospect of adversaries in Congress who do not recognize his win, analysts said. In addition, Congress has amassed significant power over government spending in the past decade, which could frustrate Lula's promises to maintain his signature welfare programs. Meanwhile, his government forecasts meager 2.3% economic growth next year, adding to fiscal challenges worsened by high interest rates and public debt that has grown past 82% of GDP, the highest since the pandemic. "On the broad macroeconomic outlook, things are not looking great," Monica de Bolle, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, said. A hostile Congress "will make it very hard to push any reform through Congress and even try to manage the budget," she said. Lula's promises to ensure minimum wage increases remain above inflation are among those that clash with growing pressure to get debt under control. Lula’s aides have also signaled he will keep pushing to curtail tax breaks, but lawmakers have repeatedly resisted measures that raise the effective tax burden. "Fiscal policy remains Lula's biggest economic challenge," said Andres Abadia, chief Latin American economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, as growing mandatory spending and high interest costs leave little room to cut deficits. Analysts said an economic crisis could even spur Lula's impeachment, with some drawing comparisons to Brazil's 2014-2016 crisis, which preceded the impeachment of Lula's ally Dilma Rousseff. "I think the campaign for Lula's impeachment begins now," said Paulo Kramer, a political scientist who worked on former President Bolsonaro's first campaign and has spoken to people close to his son. Investors [USN:L2N46C051 TEXT:"reacted nervously"] on Monday morning, sending Brazilian assets sharply lower as markets reassessed the country's fiscal outlook under Lula. SENATE STUMBLING BLOCK Congress is likely to block or slow Lula's [USN:L1N45K0U9 TEXT:"appointments to key roles"] in institutions such as the Supreme Court and the central bank, analysts say. For the first time since Brazil returned to democracy, the executive branch will be clearly at odds with the Senate, Lucas de Aragao, a partner at Brasilia-based consultancy Arko Advice, said. "Lula will have some room to negotiate in the lower house by giving centrist parties more space, but in the Senate he will have to bargain issue by issue and adjust his legislative agenda to fit what the opposition wants," Aragao added. Bolsonaro's allies in the incoming Senate have also [USN:L6N45U19L TEXT:"vowed to impeach"] Justice Alexandre de Moraes, escalating their long-running fight with a powerful judiciary that has often aligned with Lula, blocking key right-wing legislation and shaping policy on everything from Indigenous rights to the internet.

Oct 26 : Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation. CoreWeave, which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, declined 1.6 per cent, while Nebius Group fell 4 per cent and IREN lost 1.5 per cent. Shares of Applied Digital shed 2 per cent. In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX would not buy any neocloud companies, calling it "pointless".

"200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said. "Musk is correct. You're going to need another source of revenue and profits in order to finance these projects moving forward. The cost of capital is too high to make the returns attractive," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York. In an email to Reuters, a CoreWeave spokesperson said that the company continues to see opportunities to finance its growth, underscored by qualities such as "differentiated technology". Musk was not alone in flagging the risks to the sector. Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80 per cent of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032. Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns. CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30 per cent this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least $6 billion in paper profits.

item.title: Tesla owners in Slovakia welcome assisted-drive tech as EU weighs rollout across bloc
item.description: Latvia and Slovakia are the latest European countries to approve Tesla's assisted-driving software, to the delight of some local motorists who campaigned for it, though challenges remain as the rollout begins.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Latvia and Slovakia are the latest European countries to [USN:B5N45G00M TEXT:"approve"] Tesla's (TSLA.O) assisted-driving software, to the delight of some local motorists who campaigned for it, though challenges remain as the rollout begins. Latvia on Monday became the 10th European country to approve Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) software, following on the [USN:L4N4621A3 TEXT:"heels"] of Slovakia's approval of the technology earlier this month. They mark another step in Tesla's [USN:L6N41E0C3 TEXT:"push"] to bring the technology to Europe, where the company is seeking support ahead of a [USN:L6N45H0TX TEXT:"crucial vote"] that could [USN:L6N45R0YL TEXT:"pave"] the way for a broader rollout EU-wide. In Slovakia, Igor Marcek, 35, bought his own Tesla two years ago and is getting increasingly excited about the possibility of TAD, recently [USN:L6N45V0PF TEXT:"renamed"] from FSD. "At some point the car will be able to drive on its own and save us time and energy, and we will be able to maybe deal with some other things while driving," said Marcek, a financial agent and life coach in Bratislava. Still, a test drive of a Tesla installed with TAD - which has a monthly subscription of €99 ($110.92)/month per month - highlighted safety issues. While the software smoothly handled congested highway driving and traffic merges, Marcek had to manually slam on the brakes when the car failed to slow down for a closed barrier. At a Supercharger station, the car failed to steer into an open charging bay, leading Marcek to take over. "It is still a technology that is evolving so you really have to be awake there and pay attention to what the car is doing," he said. SAFETY ISSUES Tesla enthusiasts across Europe have [USN:L6N45R0YL TEXT:"mounted"] vocal campaigns to speed up deployment, often encouraged by the company and CEO Elon Musk to lobby local authorities. In Slovakia, the Tesla Owners Slovakia club - which has 1,500 registered members - organised a coordinated vehicle light show outside the transport ministry to draw regulators' attention to the technology, Marcek said. The group also contacted the Slovakian Transport Ministry following the initial [USN:L6N40W0TJ TEXT:"Dutch"] approval, and were in frequent contact with it requesting updates, the club's president, Kristian Kratochvil, said. Tesla [USN:L6N44T0P6 TEXT:"says"] that TAD can prevent collisions by more than four times and save lives, numbers that are highly contested by safety researchers. The technology has faced heightened regulatory friction across the European Union. Regulators in [USN:L6N42Q144 TEXT:"some"] countries have raised [USN:L6N45G0VU TEXT:"safety concerns"] and [USN:L6N45L0EH TEXT:"questioned"] whether drivers can stay sufficiently attentive. ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: "Retour vers le futur" au Brésil? Flavio Bolsonaro, comme jadis son père, refuse de reconnaître la victoire de Lula
item.description: Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a remporté dimanche un quatrième mandat historique.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a [USN:L5N46C021 TEXT:"remporté"] dimanche un quatrième mandat historique. Le sénateur de 45 ans conteste une décision prise dimanche soir par un juge de la Cour suprême nommé par Lula, qui a prolongé le second tour de l'élection présidentielle de deux heures en raison d’irrégularités présumées concernant le transport des électeurs. Le fils de Jair Bolsonaro a déclaré qu’il demanderait l’annulation du résultat. "Il est impossible de reconnaître les résultats de l’élection, compte tenu des circonstances dans lesquelles les événements se sont déroulés", a-t-il déclaré à des journalistes. Le président américain Donald Trump, autrefois proche allié du père Bolsonaro, a également fait part de ses doutes sur la validité du scrutin, faisant état d'une élection truquée". "Je n'ai pas pris parti, mais ça ressemble à une nouvelle élection truquée", a-t-il déclaré, sans fournir de preuves. Parallèlement, de nombreux dirigeants ont salué la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, les félicitations affluant de l'Union européenne, du Mexique, de la France, du Canada, de l'Inde et de la Russie. Les présidents de droite récemment élus en Colombie, au Pérou et au Chili ont également rejoint les rangs des dirigeants reconnaissant les résultats de dimanche, mais l'administration américaine du président Donald Trump, proche de la famille Bolsonaro, est restée silencieuse. Les investisseurs, stupéfaits par la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a déjoué les sondages, ont fait [USN:L6N46C0UL TEXT:"plonger la Bourse brésilienne"], le taux de change et la dette publique, alors que les marchés réévaluaient les perspectives budgétaires du pays. Toutefois, l’ampleur de la défaite, Bolsonaro fils accusant un retard de plus de 4 millions de voix sur Lula, rend peu probable le succès de sa tentative pour faire annuler le scrutin, selon des analystes. Sa requête est également compromise par le fait que son équipe avait elle-même demandé une prolongation des opérations de vote en raison de fortes pluies dans le sud du pays, traditionnellement conservateur. Moins de 35.000 suffrages, soit environ 0,03% du total, ont été exprimés au cours des deux heures supplémentaires de vote ordonnées par la Cour suprême, selon une analyse des registres électoraux réalisée par Pedro Burgos, professeur à l'Insper. Le refus du fils l'ancien président de reconnaître sa défaite pourrait néanmoins déclencher une vague de manifestations dans un pays où la confiance dans le système électoral et dans l’indépendance judiciaire a été mise à rude épreuve ces dernières années, estiment les observateurs. Jair Bolsonaro avait plongé le Brésil dans une profonde crise démocratique après les élections de 2022, lorsque ses partisans avaient pris d’assaut des bâtiments gouvernementaux pour protester contre le résultat. Il a par la suite été [USN:L5N3UY1NR TEXT:"condamné"] à 27 ans de prison. Il est depuis lors détenu à domicile, pour des raisons liées à son état de santé. LULA DÉFIE LES PRONOSTICS La victoire de Lula a déjoué les sondages, coupant court à une vague conservatrice en Amérique latine. Un résultat surprise qui n'est pas non plus du goût de l’administration du président américain Donald Trump, qui a oeuvré pour le retour du clan Bolsonaro au pouvoir. Les marchés financiers ont également exprimé leurs inquiétudes. Un fonds négocié en Bourse coté à Tokyo et indexé sur l’indice brésilien Bovespa (1325.T) a plongé de près de 15% lors des échanges asiatiques à l’annonce de la victoire de Lula, tandis que les analystes s’attendaient à ce que le real brésilien s’affaiblisse face au dollar américain. Lula s'était retrouvé en seconde position face à Flavio Bolsonaro au premier tour, mais il a réussi à mobiliser sa base dans l'entre-deux-tours. S’exprimant dimanche soir dans un hôtel de São Paulo, il a adopté un ton conciliant. "Je ne parlerai pas d’unité nationale, car cela ne correspond pas toujours à la réalité de ce pays. Personne n’est obligé d’apprécier le président élu, mais celui-ci a été mis en place pour gouverner au nom de tous", a-t-il souligné. Pendant la campagne, Lula, qui a 80 ans, a mis en avant son bilan en matière de lutte contre la pauvreté et les inégalités, tout en soulignant les taux historiquement bas du chômage, de l’analphabétisme et de la déforestation. Son quatrième mandat [USN:L6N46C0YC TEXT:"s'annonce difficile"]. Il devra en effet travailler au côté d’un Congrès tenu par les alliés de Bolsonaro, après une vague conservatrice aux élections législatives. Le président français Emmanuel Macron a déclaré que la France et le Brésil avaient "beaucoup à construire ensemble", tandis que la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a affirmé que "la démocratie et le multilatéralisme avaient triomphé au Brésil". Le Kremlin a salué la réélection de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et l’a félicité pour sa contribution aux relations bilatérales et au groupe des BRICS. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a félicité le dirigeant de gauche pour ses "résultats électoraux remarquables" et a déclaré qu’il se réjouissait à l’idée d’approfondir la coopération.

item.title: 楽天トラベル、顧客情報260万件に不正アクセス クレジットカード情報3.6万件
item.description: [東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 楽天グループは２６日、旅行予約サービス「楽天トラベル」の顧客情報最大２６０万件が不正...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
楽天トラベル、顧客情報260万件に不正アクセス　クレジットカード情報3.6万件 10/26 20:30 配信

２０２５年１０月撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Dado Ruvic/Illustration）

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 楽天グループは２６日、旅行予約サービス「楽天トラベル」の顧客情報最大２６０万件が不正アクセスを受けたと発表した。最大４万件については氏名やメールアドレス電話番号などが、うち最大３万６０００件はクレジットカード情報が不正アクセスを受けた。

クレジットカード情報には、発行者識別番号と下４桁、名義人名、有効期限、国際ブランド区分が含まれる。セキュリティコードは対象外だという。

不正アクセスを受けたのは、海外ホテル予約サイトのうち、シンガポール子会社が管理・運営する一部のページ。９月１０日に異常を検知し、１５日に原因を特定、１６日にシステム改修を完了したとしている。

また、楽天トラベルの多言語予約サイトも１０月２０日に不正アクセスの可能性を検知。最大８６万件の顧客メールアドレスと社内用識別番号が不正アクセスの対象となった。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：二極化鮮明な中国経済、内需主導への大胆な構造転換阻む制約 アングル：ホルムズ海峡の商船攻撃、10月は28件と過去最多 アングル：金価格、米国債利回り上昇でも4000ドル台維持　中銀の準備資産分散が下支え アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める アングル：ネタニヤフ氏、旧来の選挙戦術で「守護者」演出　ハマス攻撃で信頼回復に苦戦も 最終更新: 10/26(月) 20:30 ロイター

(Corrects paragraph 8 and graphic to additional (not total) technology spending following clarification from Deutsche Bank) By Tom Sims and Hakan Ersen FRANKFURT, Oct 26 : AI is helping Deutsche Bank cut decisions for some smaller corporate lending from weeks to just minutes, its new technology chief Marie-Jeanne Deverdun told Reuters. The project, which went live in the summer, also reduces the time taken to make some lending decisions for multinational corporations from months to weeks, said Deverdun, who joined Deutsche Bank's management board this year.

"For smaller corporates, which are less complicated in their setup and their legal structure, we're talking weeks to minutes," Deverdun said in an interview. Deverdun said Deutsche Bank is also preparing for a future when its AI agents will interact directly with clients' own agents, as lenders are drawn into the debate among technology leaders over whether AI development is moving too fast. "We are watching that debate carefully. These are very valid concerns, and, obviously, the management of cyber risk is my number one priority," she said. "We're spending a lot of resources and budget to continue to protect the bank from those new technologies and threats," she added. Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risk as lenders race to deploy the technology while balancing questions over returns and security threats. Deutsche Bank plans more than €2.5 billion ($2.80 billion) in additional technology spending between 2026 and 2028. Germany's largest lender does not disclose its total technology spending. JPMorgan is budgeting $20 billion for 2026. Banks hope AI will trim costs and boost productivity. Britain's Barclays said last week it was cutting around 5,000 jobs or 5 per cent of its workforce this year as it uses the technology. Citigroup has said AI was now developing products at lower cost and up to 40 per cent faster. Major US banks, meanwhile, have begun blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts in response to concerns that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing has said he wants to make Deutsche "a truly AI-powered bank" after his predecessor said in 2015 its systems were "disjointed, cumbersome and far too often just plain incompatible". After the Ukraine war began, Deutsche Bank had to move its tech staff out of Russia and it is still streamlining an array of platforms, although it has cited some recent progress. Deverdun said Deutsche Bank had built an internal AI platform known as ADA, named after computing pioneer Ada Lovelace, to develop, monitor and control AI agents. ADA allows the bank to oversee agent activity, manage risk and switch between AI models as technology evolves, she said. "We're already preparing for an agentic economy where our agents interact with the agents of our clients with clear accountability and the right controls," she added. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

Source: Reuters

item.title: 中国人民銀、ノンバンクの大量解約に備え流動性供給制度
item.description: [北京／上海 ２６日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２６日、大規模な解約に直面するノンバンク金融機関に緊...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国人民銀、ノンバンクの大量解約に備え流動性供給制度 10/26 20:21 配信

北京の中国人民銀行本部、2025年5月撮影 REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

[北京／上海 ２６日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２６日、大規模な解約に直面するノンバンク金融機関に緊急流動性を供給するスワップ制度の創設を発表した。国内債券市場の安定維持への取り組みの一環。

人民銀によると、資産運用会社が集団的な流動性リスクに直面した場合や債券市場がシステミックなストレスにさらされた時などに発動する。

こうした状況下では、金融システム上重要な理財部門や投資信託運用会社とその親会社が人民銀から中央銀行手形を借り入れ、市場でのレポ取引を通じて資金を調達できる。調達資金で適格債券や、解約に直面する自社の投資信託商品の受益権を購入し、これらの資産を人民銀に担保として差し入れる仕組みだ。

人民銀の潘功勝総裁は先週、国家金融監督管理総局と中国証券監督管理委員会と連携し、ノンバンク金融機関の大規模な解約に対応する流動性支援策を導入すると表明していた。

item.title: Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta Platforms said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion. The Facebook parent has launched public offerings worth about $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and said it also plans to launch a separate at-the-market share sale program worth up to $60 billion. The company will launch the larger share sale program after its new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but said it has not yet finalized its timing and terms of the sale. Meta's fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) for Class A shares. Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers. Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic. "We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts said in a note. "Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity." The company's shares fell about 1.4% in morning trading. The latest fundraising further underscores a shift among big technology companies increasingly [USN:L6N3WU0Q5 TEXT:"tapping debt markets and raising equity"] to bolster their AI infrastructure, having previously relied on cash to fund their investments. Earlier this year, [USN:L4N42B1AK TEXT:"Alphabet increased the size"] of its equity offerings to $84.75 billion. Separately on Monday, SpaceX said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"about $40 billion"]. META'S AI SPENDING IS BURNING CASH Meta has committed to spend about $825 billion in the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centers, AI-related infrastructure and cloud computing power. But the aggressive expansion has eroded its historically strong free cash flow. The company reported a $2.12 billion cash burn in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in over a decade, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year ago. Still, the early popularity of [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"its consumer-focused AI agent Muse"] and release of a competitive new [USN:L4N45Y13Q TEXT:"series of AI models"] have helped partly justify Meta's aggressive investments. "We believe that Meta will ultimately produce a profitable AI business and its returns longer-term should help the company diversify, although the path may not be linear," William Blair analysts said. The company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $82.45 billion and long-term debt of $80.92 billion as of September 30, according to its latest quarterly filing. Last week, Meta raised the lower end of its annual [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"capital expenditure"] forecast to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion. The company has said it would issue Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta [USN:L6N46801B TEXT:"agreed to grant Zuckerberg Class C shares"] that he can sell to help pay a potential California billionaire wealth tax, in exchange for a commitment to keep him in California.

Oct 26 : Verizon raised its annual forecast for wireless subscriber additions on Monday, betting on strong demand for its simplified plans, and signed an AI infrastructure deal worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services.  For the third quarter, the telecom carrier reported nearly double the analysts' estimate for gains in monthly-bill paying wireless subscribers at 406,000, against Visible Alpha expectations of 209,439. • Verizon now expects to add between 1.1 million and 1.2 million postpaid phone subscribers this year compared with earlier projections of 750,000 to 1 million • It also raised its full-year adjusted earnings per share forecast to $5.04 to $5.06, from $4.99 to $5.04 earlier

item.title: Barril cae ante esperanzas de paz, ataques a Arabia Saudita limitan las pérdidas
item.description: Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Cavale
item.content:encoded: Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses. * Los futuros del crudo Brent bajaron 91 centavos, o un 0,8%, a 115,81 dólares, mientras que los futuros del West Texas Intermediate (WTI) cayeron 1,51 dólares, o un 1,46%, a 101,76 dólares por barril. * Ambos referenciales retrocedieron tras las fuertes ganancias registradas el viernes, cuando el Brent cerró con un alza de más de 3 dólares para acumular un incremento semanal del 6%, mientras que el WTI avanzó un 2,3% en la semana. * La atención de los inversores siguió centrada en la escalada de tensiones en Oriente Medio, después de que los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, dijeron haber atacado estaciones de bombeo del oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudita, así como el aeropuerto de Riad, durante el fin de semana. * Arabia Saudita informó el domingo que había interceptado más misiles y drones; por su parte, la coalición liderada por los saudíes comunicó el lunes la destrucción de tres drones que tenían como objetivo Riad y las regiones meridionales del reino. * En una medida que podría involucrar a Egipto de manera más directa en el conflicto, el Parlamento autorizó al presidente Abdel Fattah al-Sisi a adoptar "todas las medidas necesarias" para ayudar a Arabia Saudita a defenderse. Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán mantuvieron conversaciones con funcionarios iraníes en Teherán, como parte de los esfuerzos para evitar una mayor escalada en la región. EL encuentro supuso el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y las tres naciones, que firmaron un pacto de defensa mutua en agosto. Al término, los cuatro países acordaron continuar las conversaciones con el objetivo de reforzar la cooperación en materia de paz y seguridad, informaron los medios estatales iraníes.

item.title: 独ＩＦＯ業況指数、10月90.2で予想以上に改善 先行きを楽観視
item.description:
Maria Martinez
[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] - ドイツのＩＦＯ経済研究所が２６日発表した１０月の業況...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独ＩＦＯ業況指数、10月90.2で予想以上に改善　先行きを楽観視 10/26 19:50 配信

ベルリンの街並み、6月撮影 REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch

Maria Martinez

[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] - ドイツのＩＦＯ経済研究所が２６日発表した１０月の業況指数は、先行きへの楽観的な見方が強まったことで、市場予想以上に改善した。改善は６カ月連続。

業況指数は９０．２と、９月の８９．９から上昇した。ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は９０．０だった。

期待指数は９月の９０．４から９１．６に上昇した。

ＩＦＯのクレメンス・フュースト所長は「景気回復は続いている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏によると、１０月の企業の先行きに対する楽観度は４年半超ぶりの高水準となった。

ドイツ政府は経済成長率予想を引き上げ２０２６年が１．３％、２７年が１．１％とした。４月時点では０．５％、０．９％と予想していた。

ハンブルク商業銀行のチーフエコノミスト、サイラス・デラルビア氏は「ＩＦＯ業況指数が６カ月連続で上昇したことは、数多くの逆風にもかかわらずドイツ経済が成長軌道にあることを示唆している」と述べた。

第３・四半期の成長率は３０日に発表される。

キャピタル・エコノミクスは、ここ数カ月でＩＦＯなど一部の企業調査が改善したものの、第３・四半期はゼロ成長にとどまったと予想している。ただ欧州担当チーフエコノミスト、アンドリュー・ケニンガム氏は「労働市場の回復の兆しや財政刺激策の継続と併せ、今回の調査は第３・四半期の一時的な低迷が一過性の要因にもよるもので、第４・四半期は成長を取り戻すというわれわれの見方を裏付けている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのギッツェル氏によると、景況感の改善は全て製造業によるもの。好調な受注と政府のインフラ基金の効果が表れ始め、製造業の景況感を明確に押し上げているという。一方でサービス業は企業の楽観的な見方が後退、家計の消費支出の低迷が原因とみられるという。

ＩＮＧのマクロ調査グローバル責任者、カーステン・ブジェスキ氏は「今回の指数は、ドイツ経済の先行きを巡り継続中の財政刺激策の効果が経済全体に一段と波及することが、引き続き期待されていることを示している」と述べた。

メルツ首相は経済再生に向け、通常予算とは別枠で５０００億ユーロ（５６００億ドル）規模のインフラ基金を創設した。また、軍備増強に向け、憲法に定める借り入れ制限「債務ブレーキ」を見直した。

＜現況判断は悪化＞

期待指数の上昇が業況指数全体を押し上げた一方、現況に対する評価はやや悪化した。現況指数は前月の８９．５から８８．８に低下した。

デラルビア氏は、原油・ガス価格の大幅な上昇が電力価格の上昇や株式市場のボラティリティーにもつながっており、企業に打撃を与えるのは間違いないと指摘。さらに「ドイツ企業にとって２番目に重要な輸出先であるフランス経済が、政治的混乱や債券市場の動揺によってほぼ停滞したままとなれば、その影響はドイツにも及ぶ」との見方を示した。

コメルツ銀行のエコノミスト、イェルク・クレーマー氏は、さまざまなリスクにもかかわらず、ドイツ経済の回復は続く公算が大きいと指摘。ただ「抜本的な改革の欠如、トランプ氏の関税、中国の輸出攻勢により、回復は緩やかなものにとどまるだろう」との見方を示した。

item.title: 米年末商戦の配送料過去最高へ、軽油高騰にサーチャージ算出変更が拍車
item.description:
Lisa Baertlein
［ロサンゼルス ２６日 ロイター］ - 今年の米国年末商戦の小口貨物配送料金は過去最高と...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米年末商戦の配送料過去最高へ、軽油高騰にサーチャージ算出変更が拍車 10/26 19:47 配信

フェデックスの配送トラック、米ワシントンDCで2024年撮影 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/File Photo

Lisa Baertlein

［ロサンゼルス　２６日　ロイター］ - 今年の米国年末商戦の小口貨物配送料金は過去最高となる見通しだ。ディーゼル燃料（軽油）価格の高騰でＵＰＳとフェデックスが燃油サーチャージを引き上げており、米小売業者に逆風が吹いている。しかし、配送コスト上昇は、単純に燃料価格の問題だけではなさそうだ。そこには運送会社のサーチャージ算出方法変更という要因が働いているという。

年末商戦に関連する荷物量は第４・四半期に倍増することもある。大手小売業者を含む荷主１８００社の匿名化データを分析したＴＤコーエン／ＡＦＳ貨物指数によると、同四半期の陸送料金は、ネット通販購入品を含め、前年同期比で５．８％上昇、速達便は１３．８％上昇する見通しだ。同指数は、小口貨物のコストは重量やサイズ、配送先によって異なるため、金額ではなく変化率を示している。

米エネルギー情報局（ＥＩＡ）によると、１０月１９日時点の米国の路上用ディーゼル燃料の平均価格は１ガロン＝６．２８ドルだった。米国とイスラエルが２月２８日にイランを攻撃して以降、６５％上昇したことになる。

ＡＦＳロジスティクスのチーフアナリティクスオフィサー、ミンシュ・ベイツ氏は「燃料は誰にとっても最大の関心事だが、良い材料は見当たらない」と述べた。

＜運送会社の算出方法変更がコスト押し上げ＞

小売業者が頭を痛める輸送コスト。拍車をかけているのは、運送会社の算出方法の変更だ。

ベイツ氏によると、燃油サーチャージコストのうち軽油価格の上昇による分は３０％弱にすぎない。ＵＰＳやフェデックスなど業界大手が算出方法を変更したことにより、サーチャージは燃料価格よりもはるかに速いペースで上昇し、燃料価格が上がらない場合でも上昇しているという。

例えば、２０２１年第１・四半期に軽油価格が２．９１ドルだった時、同指数で燃油サーチャージは基本配送料金の７．７５％だった。仮に軽油価格がこの水準まで下がったとしても、現在の燃油サーチャージは２３．７５％と約３倍になる。燃油サーチャージの算出方法の変更が運送会社の収入を増やし、小売業者のコストを押し上げる構図だ。

各社のサーチャージ表に基づくと、ＥＩＡの平均価格である６．２８ドルでは、ＵＰＳの燃油サーチャージは２９．５％、フェデックスは２９％となる。

ＵＰＳは、料金設定は同社の質の高いサービスとインフラ投資を反映していると説明した。フェデックスはコメント要請に応じていない。両社は今週、四半期決算を発表する予定だ。

重いサーチャージ負担を小売業者はただ受け入れているだけなのか。

オントラック、ゴーフォー、ユニユニ、ジツ、ビーホなどは急成長中の配送会社だ。配送追跡・管理会社シップマトリックスのサティッシュ・ジンデル社長によると、米国の人口の約７０％をカバーしており、年末商戦期の荷物量の増加に対応するため、輸送能力も増強している。「輸送費を減らしたい多くの荷主に採用されている」という。

とはいえ、こうした企業の一部も高額な燃油サーチャージを導入している。オントラックが公開しているサーチャージ表によると、１０月２５日までの１週間の同社の西海岸のサーチャージは２９．５％だった。

輸送コストを抑えるために、米郵政公社（ＵＳＰＳ）やアマゾン・ドット・コムの物流部門を使う手もある。ＵＳＰＳは４月、大半の荷物に初めて８％の燃油サーチャージを課した。アマゾンも同じ月に、出品者向けのフルフィルメント手数料に３．５％の燃料・物流関連サーチャージを上乗せし始めた。

ただ配送会社の切り替えにはデメリットもあるとアナリストは指摘する。配送を複数社に分けると取扱量に応じた割引効果がなくなる可能性がある。また、年末商戦期の配送計画は数カ月前に決まるため、直前の変更は難しいという。ＪＰモルガンのアナリストは、アマゾンが近いうちにＵＰＳとフェデックスの市場支配を崩す可能性は低いとの見方を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：二極化鮮明な中国経済、内需主導への大胆な構造転換阻む制約 アングル：ホルムズ海峡の商船攻撃、10月は28件と過去最多 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か 最終更新: 10/26(月) 19:47 ロイター

item.title: Oro sube ya que menores precios del crudo alivian temores sobre inflación previo Fed
item.description: El precio del oro subió el lunes, recuperándose tras haber alcanzado en la sesión previa su nivel más bajo en más de tres meses, a medida que el descenso en los precios del petróleo moderaba las preocupaciones sobre la inflación, justo antes de la reunión de la Reserva Federal de esta semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel John
item.content:encoded: El precio del oro subió el lunes, recuperándose tras haber alcanzado en la sesión previa su nivel más bajo en más de tres meses, a medida que el descenso en los precios del petróleo moderaba las preocupaciones sobre la inflación, justo antes de la reunión de la Reserva Federal de esta semana. * El oro al contado ganó un 0,6% a 4.020,60 dólares por onza a las 1809 GMT, tras haber tocado el viernes los 3.975 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde el 20 de julio. Los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos con entrega en diciembre cerraron con un alza del 0,8%, a 4.038,40 dólares por onza. * "Se ha producido un ligero retroceso en el precio del crudo, lo que está beneficiando al oro; además, ha surgido cierto interés por comprar a precios más bajos", señaló Bob Haberkorn, estratega sénior de mercado en StoneX. "Creo que el volumen de negociación será moderado y que nos mantendremos cerca del nivel de los 4.000 dólares hasta que la Reserva Federal haga su anuncio, para ver qué tienen que decir". * Los precios del petróleo caían tras el fuerte repunte de la semana pasada, aunque se mantenían cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses, en medio de esperanzas de una disminución de las hostilidades entre Estados Unidos e Irán. * El retroceso del petróleo ha aliviado algunas preocupaciones sobre la inflación. Sin embargo, los mercados siguen cautelosos ante la posibilidad de nuevas interrupciones en el suministro que podrían reactivar las presiones sobre los precios. * La decisión de la Fed sobre las tasas se conocerá el miércoles. Se espera, de forma generalizada, una pausa tras la subida de septiembre, mientras que las expectativas de un nuevo incremento en diciembre se sitúan en el 80%, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. * Unas tasas más altas aumentan el costo de oportunidad de mantener oro, que no rinde intereses. * Los futuros del crudo Brent bajaban un 2%, a cerca de 114 dólares el barril, tras alcanzar la semana pasada su máximo en seis meses. * Los inversionistas también esperan la publicación, el 29 de octubre, de los datos sobre los gastos de consumo personal (PCE) de Estados Unidos, el indicador que la Fed sigue más de cerca para ver si la inflación se aproxima a su objetivo del 2%. * Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado subió un 0,4%, a 54,11 dólares por onza; el platino bajó un 1,1% a 1.533,65 dólares por onza; y el paladio sumó un 0,5% a 1.049,09 dólares por onza.

item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 26 : US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies. One Powerpoint presentation proposed a strategy for
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Exclusive-US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters

A person walks in front of a polling station on the first day of early voting in New Jersey State, in Harrison, New Jersey, US, October 24, 2026. REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 26 : US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies.  One Powerpoint presentation proposed a strategy for Mike Minogue, Republican challenger to Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey. It aimed to convince ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other chatbots to present him as the preferred choice on key issues, and went well beyond traditional search-engine optimization that candidates have used for years. As AI increasingly becomes a source of news, political campaigns must make greater efforts to control its output and become its recommendation when voters ask questions such as who is best on issues like taxes, housing and public safety. Some experts worry about fact-checking and misinformation in AI campaigns. Fees can range from hundreds of dollars a month for small AI monitoring jobs to tens of thousands per month if consulting and buying media are included.

The presentation proposed that Minogue's campaign should create hundreds of AI-friendly policy pages and citations across the websites frequently cited by AI chatbots. It proposed ways to track how major chatbots respond to political questions, and systematically alter content until the answers reflect the candidate's platform. At the center of the pitch was the idea that in addition to persuading voters directly, campaigns can increasingly shape the information environment by feeding the internet, and AI assistants, data that influences how candidates are described, compared and recommended.  "Campaigns using AI-influence training are now a reality that we face and it will be ubiquitous by the 2028 cycle," which will include a presidential election, said Joe Bonilla, managing partner of Relentless Awareness. The New York-based creative strategy firm has worked with companies and political candidates at the federal, state, and local levels. "The public increasingly cannot and will not be able to discern what is created by systems like Claude and ChatGPT versus human-originated content," Bonilla said. The Powerpoint presentation prepared for Minogue's campaign and seen by Reuters describes generative engine optimization, or GEO, the AI-era successor to search engine optimization (SEO). It says the firm would buy placements on high-authority websites that AI models already cite. It would also produce YouTube and Reddit content and publish issue pages built to be picked up by chatbots. "When the campaign is ready, we run paid placements on high-domain-authority sites the LLMs (large language models) already cite — plus Reddit, which is disproportionately weighted in retrieval," the pitch deck says. VOTERS ASK CHATBOTS As online election information has surged, some 25 per cent of eligible voters have asked a chatbot about a political candidate when deciding how to vote, according to Cameron Hickey, CEO of the National Conference on Citizenship. "If you don't put the right information out there, who knows what the AI engines are going to grab onto," said Thomas Howell, CEO of Visigent, the Austin, Texas-based firm that wrote the strategy document for Minogue. Visigent has six political campaigns among its clients, but Howell would not identify his clients. The Minogue campaign did not return calls and emails requesting comment. Campaigns must now compete to become "the recommendation inside the AI answer" according to the presentation prepared for Minogue. "We are just at the beginning of this new era," said Meg Schwenzfeier with Caucus AI, which tracks voter usage of AI. "This year the focus has been on candidates ensuring their own websites surface in chatbot results," she said. But she warned "chatbots speak very authoritatively and can consume vast amounts of unvetted information, so we have to guard against misinformation."  FROM SEO TO GEO  Fees for AI strategists are tied to "AI recommendation share," meaning how often chatbots return the candidate in a response.  Visigent's website offers software for $134 a month and up to $9,000 monthly for large clients who require editorial design and development services. On the political side, Howell said fees start at $5,000 a month, but "if we also are going to be building paid media or paid placements or reaching out and doing any sort of influencer outreach or anything that is pay-for-play," fees could reach $50,000 a month. These fees are expected to rise, Howell said, as the 2028 presidential cycle kicks off after the midterm elections. The presentation shows the top success fee of $200,000 for a "category win." CampSight, another option geared toward progressive candidates, says it has helped younger candidates run for offices from school board to state legislature. CampSight, operated by Run for Something Action Fund, charges campaigns between $9 and $250 per month for information on what LLMs are saying about them and tips on influencing them. For statewide and federal campaigns pricing is "custom" and includes a "dedicated strategist." "When we started this project last summer, we were monitoring AI answers on some of our Run for Something candidates and we were seeing things that were said on Reddit appearing in AI answers the next day," Jordan Haines, the Run for Something Chief Technology Officer told Reuters. "This year, that dark fear hasn't really come to fruition. I think that the LLMs have been pretty savvy about discerning accurate and reputable information from non-reputable information." Run For Something's president Amanda Litman said in a post on X that dozens of campaigns use CampSight, with more than 300 candidates and organizations on its waiting list.

Source: Reuters
